Whole-brain analyses and voxel coordinates are reported (including exploratory whole-brain results and specific MNI coordinates for group effects), and ROI analyses are complemented by small-volume corrections; processing details (SPM8) and MR field strength (3.0 T) are provided. Participant information and demographics are described (groups matched on age and sex), and cue type is cocaine. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related 3T fMRI study using visual cues (game screenshots and smoking images) and reports within-participant contrasts (gaming>neutral and smoking>neutral). Group-level, random-effects whole-brain activation maps for each group were obtained (thresholded at p<0.05 FDR) and reported in the text (regions and BA values), and conjunction analyses identify common activations. Relevant metadata are provided (participant sex/age description, cue types including nicotine and gaming, scanner field strength 3T, and processing software SPM5). Thus it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity fMRI, within-subject contrasts, whole-brain group maps (reported in text/figures), and requisite participant and acquisition details.

This is a protocol/design paper for a randomized controlled trial that describes planned fMRI procedures but reports no original task-evoked fMRI data or group-level whole-brain statistical maps. Additionally, the cue paradigm uses personalized auditory imagery scripts (audio cues) rather than visual stimuli, so it does not meet the requirement for cue-reactivity with visual stimuli. Therefore it does not provide the within-participant drug-cue>control visual contrast maps or whole-brain task activation maps required for inclusion. Exclusion is based primarily on E6 (non-empirical/protocol paper without original human fMRI results). It also fails I3 (visual-stimulus cue modality) and I5/I4 (no reported within-subject cue>control whole-brain maps or analyses).

This is a within-subject fMRI study of smokers using visual smoking videos versus neutral videos, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported. Methods report scanner field strength (3 T), processing software (fmristat), participant ages and sex, and contrasts of smoking>neutral were analyzed and reported with whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI investigation of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using standardized visual pictorial stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts of smoking-related > neutral cues. It includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects, cluster-corrected Z-statistics) showing activation in several regions and reports coordinates and ROI analyses. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are all explicitly reported. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues with a within-subject Heroin>Neutral contrast and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses. Whole-brain task activations are reported (voxelwise, FDR-corrected) with coordinates in MNI space. Participant demographics (male, age range), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity meta-analysis and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of withdrawal-induced craving and structural DTI correlates; it does not present any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural-reward cues. There is no within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control stimuli or any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps; analyses are ICA and ACC-seeded resting-state functional connectivity (seed-based rsFC). Therefore it violates the meta-analysis inclusion requirements and meets exclusion criterion E4 (resting-state/seed-based connectivity only, with no whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward (food) cues with healthy adult female participants (ages reported). The within-subject contrast food vs. non-food (control) images is explicitly reported. The paper describes group-level whole-brain activation analyses to food vs. non-food images (reported in the Supplementary material), satisfying the whole-brain/map requirement (I5/I6). Relevant details are provided: participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Although primary hypothesis testing used anatomical ROIs (NAcc, vmPFC), whole-brain results are performed and referenced. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an ASL fMRI study using cocaine-related videos, but its primary analyses are seed-based functional connectivity and wavelet transform coherence between amygdala and dorsal cingulate during an attempted craving-inhibition task. It does not report a within-participant task contrast of drug cues > control stimuli, nor does it present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map (only seed-based whole-brain regression/connectivity maps). Therefore it does not meet the requirement for a task-evoked whole-brain activation contrast and is excluded under E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with a within-participant contrast of high-calorie (HC) vs low-calorie (LC) food cues. Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses were reported (repeated-measures ANOVAs with cluster-level FWE correction) using SPM12 on a 3T scanner. Participant demographic information (age, sex) and cue type (food) are provided. The study also reports additional connectivity (PPI) analyses, but crucially includes unmasked whole-brain task activation maps/analyses rather than only ROI or connectivity results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts of reward cues versus neutral cues and provides required methodological details (participants’ sex/age, scanner field strength, processing software), it does not assess drug cues or natural reward-related cues (e.g., food or sexual stimuli). The task used monetary incentive delay with geometric cues predicting monetary gain/loss, i.e., monetary reward anticipation rather than drug-cue or specified natural-reward cue-reactivity. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control). Whole-text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E3–E6) directly apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It contains within-participant smoking>neutral contrasts and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (random-effects GLM and mixed-effects ANCOVA) with cluster correction. Methods report participant sex (women), age comparisons, cue type (smoking/nicotine), MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX), satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that uses visual stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs control pictures/odors and habituation terms) and examines pre- and post-treatment differences, and group-level mixed-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Z-scores, cluster-wise FWE correction). Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, alcohol cue type, 3T scanner, FSL processing). Results are reported as whole-brain task-evoked maps and described in the text with statistical thresholds and cluster-level inference. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task effects, empirical human fMRI data). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

Although the study uses an fMRI reward-cue antisaccade task with visual monetary cues (reward vs neutral) and reports within-subject reward>neutral contrasts and adequate methodological details (age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner, FSL), the paper only reports ROI-based results. The authors state whole-brain analyses were run but no whole-brain clusters were identified beyond a priori ROIs, and they report only ROI results. This meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results). Therefore it does not satisfy the meta-analysis requirement for a reported group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map (I5). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, reporting within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses performed in SPM (SPM5/SPM8) on data acquired at 3T. Whole-brain activation results are described (and illustrated) in the text and used in subsequent ROI/correlation and Cox regression analyses. Relevant participant information (age range, sex/gender representation discussion), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are reported. The paper is empirical, not solely ROI- or connectivity-based, and provides task-evoked whole-brain maps/analyses, satisfying inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I7: the provided full text does not report participant age and sex (demographics appear to be referenced in missing tables/figures). It does meet I3 (fMRI study of natural reward — food — using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrasts: appetizing > non-food and appetizing > bland), I5 (group-level whole-brain analyses were performed and reported at whole-brain uncorrected threshold and in a supplemental table), and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears to contain core sections (intro, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is set to false.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study using visual cannabis cues (meets I3, I5, I6, I7). However, the primary reported analyses are an approach-bias contrast [(approach-cannabis + avoid-control) > (avoid-cannabis + approach-control)] and condition > baseline contrasts. The paper does not report a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., cannabis > control) as a group-level whole-brain task contrast, which fails inclusion criterion I4. Because all inclusion criteria must be met, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s core inclusion criteria. It is a PET molecular imaging study measuring mu-opioid receptor binding and treatment outcome, not an fMRI task study of cue-reactivity using visual drug/natural reward cues. There is no within-participant task contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli, no task-evoked fMRI whole-brain activation maps, and no visual cue-reactivity paradigm. Although the full text is complete and reports participant demographics and voxelwise PET (SPM) analyses, these do not satisfy I3 (fMRI), I4 (within-participant cue>control task contrast), or I5 (task-evoked whole-brain fMRI activation map).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using visual natural reward (food) cues and reports within-subject contrasts of high-calorie (natural reward) versus non-food control stimuli. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented (contrasts thresholded and corrected for whole-brain multiple comparisons) and described in the text and results tables/figures. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with an explicit within-participant contrast of food>scrambled control images. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task effects (food vs. control) and voxelwise results (main effect of task and correlations), provides coordinate tables and SPM analyses, and reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This study is an rTMS clinical trial that used structural MRI for neuronavigation but did not acquire or report task-based functional MRI activation maps. It does not assess fMRI cue-reactivity or report any within-participant drug-cue > control whole-brain contrasts. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity (I3 and I4) and provides no whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or coordinates (I5/I6). The full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on absence of task-based fMRI cue-reactivity data rather than on non-empirical status.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task analyses (2×2 ANOVA and smoking–neutral contrast) with cluster-wise correction and presents whole-brain results/maps. Imaging details and processing software are reported (3.0T Philips scanner; AFNI). Participant characteristics (male adult smokers, n=32; descriptive statistics referenced) and cue type are provided. The study also reports additional connectivity analyses, but critically includes whole-brain task-evoked activation maps, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with a within-subject contrast (appetitive > neutral) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses. The paper reports brain activation maps/clusters (with voxelwise thresholds and cluster sizes) and provides necessary methodological details (participant sex and age comparisons, cue type: food, 3T scanner, BrainVoyager processing). Results include coordinates/regions and statistical values and correlations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study in alcohol-dependent patients using visual alcohol images, with within-subject contrasts (alcohol>neutral). The paper includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain thresholds and reported clusters/coordinates) in addition to ROI tests. Key methodological details are reported (participant sex/age range, cue type = alcohol, 3-T scanner, SPM5/8 preprocessing), satisfying reporting requirements. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-subject task activation maps).

This is an fMRI study of emotional (negative face) processing and its correlation with cigarette use, not a cue-reactivity task using drug- or natural-reward-related visual cues. It therefore fails inclusion criterion I3 (not assessing drug/natural reward cue-reactivity). Additionally, the reported analyses are ROI-based insula extractions and correlations; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps for drug/natural cue>control are reported, invoking exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) with within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs neutral/abstract) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with coordinates and cluster results. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The manuscript includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it meets all stated inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate listed exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual (and auditory) stimuli, reporting within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM. Methods report scanner field strength (1.5T), processing software (SPM5), participant age/sex, and cue type (food). Statistical thresholds and cluster-correction procedures are described and whole-brain activation results are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Thus the study meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual-cue fMRI studies of natural reward cue-reactivity.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking > neutral cues and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (FLAME, cluster-corrected) for the smoking vs. neutral contrast. Relevant methodological and participant details are provided (age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, FSL processing). The whole-brain results are described in the text and compared to a DMN ROI; beta-weights were extracted and correlated with MRS measures. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study is not a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual drug or natural reward cues. It reports arterial spin labeling (CBF) measurements during rest and a spatial working-memory task in abstinent alcoholic men, with no presentation of drug/food/sexual cues and no within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control stimuli. While whole-brain CBF maps are reported for rest and working-memory conditions, these are not cue-reactivity task-evoked maps required by the review. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I7. The full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues in chronic smokers. It reports within-subject contrasts of aversive smoking-related > neutral and appetitive smoking-related > neutral, and group-level random-effects whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (SPM5) with cluster correction (AFNI 3dClustSim). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0 T) and processing software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies and provides whole-brain results reported in the text/tables.

This is an fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay task (visual cues signaling potential monetary reward), i.e., natural reward-related visual stimuli. The analyses include within-participant contrasts of gain versus nongain (reward-related cues > control), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected and less stringent whole-brain results). Results are reported in text/tables and ROI/whole-brain analyses; processing software (SPM2) and participant demographics (matched on age and gender) are provided. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for cue type, within-subject contrasts, whole-brain maps (reported), and reporting format. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study does not meet the key inclusion criterion I3 because cue-reactivity was elicited using gustatory (taste) stimuli delivered via a gustometer (alcohol vs lychee juice), not visual stimuli. It does meet several other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant alcohol>control contrast), I5/I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported and corrected; results described in text/tables/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type [alcohol], scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [FSL, FreeSurfer] reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are triggered. Because the meta-analysis specifically requires visual cue paradigms (I3), this study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related images) with a within-participant contrast (smoking > neutral). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster-corrected) comparing smoking vs neutral images and further reports ROI and ICA results. Key methodological details required by the review are present: cue type (nicotine), participant sex (women only), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). The whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/results are described in the text and corrected for multiple comparisons. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high- vs low-caloric food images). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., high-caloric > low-caloric in Tea and Water conditions and interaction contrasts) and conducted exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses and ROI analyses; whole-brain results are described in text and supplementary materials. Participant age/sex (young adult women), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual cigarette images (meets I3 and I4; participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and software are reported meeting I7). However, all primary statistical tests reported are region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (a priori anatomically defined ROIs and ROI-based hypothesis testing). The manuscript does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain results. Therefore it reports only ROI results with no whole-brain activation map, violating inclusion criterion I5 and meeting exclusion criterion E3.

This is an empirical BOLD-fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of food vs. non-food control stimuli, and includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR cluster-corrected) in addition to ROI analyses. The paper provides participant age and sex, cue type (food), MRI scanner details (MAGNETOM Prisma, methods note optimization at 3T), and processing software (FSL). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual food images (a natural reward) and reports within-subject contrasts comparing craved food cues to control stimuli (Look Craved > Look Not Craved; Look Craved > Look Neutral). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected results and peak coordinates), with processing details (SPM12b, AFNI/AlphaSim), scanner field strength (3.0 T Siemens Skyra), and participant demographics (ages 10–23, all female) provided. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity (I3, I4) and the requirements for whole-brain reporting and methodological details (I5–I7). No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking-related and affective cues and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking>neutral, positive>neutral), and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, all group-level statistical testing was conducted within an a priori anatomical mask (an inclusive AAL ROI mask) rather than as an unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map. Because the paper reports only masked/ROI-constrained voxelwise results (i.e., no unmasked whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), it does not meet the review’s whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and thus falls under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so exclusion is based on analytic approach rather than missing information.

This is an fMRI study of visual food-cue reactivity (natural reward) and includes within-subject contrasts of food vs. object stimuli, but the fMRI analyses and results are reported as ROI-based COPE extractions and ROI-wise mixed-effects models. The paper does not present or describe any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps, nor tables of whole-brain coordinates or whole-brain figures; therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of appetitive (natural food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (pictures) with within-subject contrasts (CS+ vs CS−) reported during an fMRI reinstatement test. Group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses were conducted (flexible factorial model) and whole-brain results/coordinates are reported (MNI peaks given; exploratory whole-brain maps described). Relevant details are provided: participant age/sex, cue type (food), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (SPM12). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group only, or non-empirical) apply.

The study does not meet I3: it is not an fMRI study of drug cues or of the natural reward cue types specified for the review (e.g., food or sexual cues). The fMRI component used monetary reward cues (secondary reinforcer) in an incentive-conflict task rather than drug-related cues or the natural reward types targeted by the meta-analysis. The paper does, however, include within-participant contrasts of rewarded vs nonrewarded stimuli (meets I4), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps (meets I5), and presents coordinate-based results/whole-brain activations (meets I6). Reporting of participant demographics and some methodological details is present but the cue type (monetary) falls outside the review’s defined cue domains. Because I3 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded per the protocol.

This study is an empirical pupillometry (eye-tracking) study of cue-reactivity in alcohol-dependent patients and does not use functional MRI. It therefore fails the primary inclusion criterion I3 (must be an fMRI study). Consequently it cannot satisfy I4–I7 (within-subject fMRI contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise maps, MRI scanner/processing details). Full text appears complete. No fMRI data, whole-brain results, or MRI methods are reported, so the study is not eligible for a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity.

This study is a resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity comparison between alcohol dependence and internet gaming disorder, not a task-based cue-reactivity fMRI study using visual drug or natural reward cues. It does not include any within-participant contrasts of drug-cue > control stimuli or a task-evoked whole-brain activation map. Therefore it violates the review’s inclusion requirements and meets exclusion criteria for resting-state/seed-based studies without task activation and for reporting only group comparisons without an unmasked whole-brain task effect.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) and reports group-level whole-brain analyses with sufficient participant and scanner details, it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward cues versus an independent control stimulus (e.g., non-reward/neutral images). The reported contrasts compare cognitive strategies (up-regulation, suppression, reappraisal) and passive viewing of the same food images rather than food cues > control-stimuli contrasts required by the meta-analysis (I4). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 and must be excluded.

This article is a symposium/review summarizing multiple human laboratory studies (IV alcohol self-administration, cortisol/ACTH, clinical data) rather than reporting an original task-based fMRI experiment with visual drug/natural reward cues. The text does not present a within-participant contrast of drug-cues>control with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables required for inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical/review without original human fMRI data). The full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cues and includes within-participant contrasts (fattening > nonfattening) and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL, FreeSurfer, AFNI), satisfying I3, I4, and I7. However, the paper uses an a priori ROI approach and reports ROI/global-average and ROI-specific results. There is no clear report of an unmasked, group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or coordinates for whole-brain results; analyses and results are ROI-focused. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) with within-subject contrasts (high-calorie foods>objects; low-calorie foods>objects). Group-level second-level random-effects analyses were performed; authors state they conducted whole-brain analyses (reported at P<0.001 FWE-corrected) in addition to ROI small-volume corrections. Relevant participant information (female, ages 19–28), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies and no exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study (study 1) that probes neural cue-reactivity to palatable food using visual cues (milkshake image) and tastant delivery. It includes within-participant contrasts (anticipatory food cue > anticipatory tasteless-solution cue and receipt contrasts), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-level q-FDR corrected) with peak coordinates and effect sizes. Methods report participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (Siemens Allegra 3T), and processing software (SPM12). Full article text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of real smoking decisions with stress manipulations and in-scanner e-cigarette puffs, not a visual cue-reactivity paradigm. Although whole-brain analyses are reported and participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and analysis software (AFNI) are provided, the task does not present drug-related visual cues nor report a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli. Thus it fails the core inclusion requirements for cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3 and I4). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion is based on not meeting required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis scope.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smokers using visual pictorial smoking cues and neutral controls. It reports within-subject contrasts contrasting smoking vs neutral pictures (LCSP minus LCNP) and a cue-exposure-corrected attention contrast, and conducts group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise analyses with coordinates and Z-values. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3,I4,I5,I6,and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (food) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and adequate reporting of age/sex, scanner field strength and processing software, it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food images). The reported contrasts compare task instructions applied to the same food cues (inhibition vs. passive viewing, imaginary eating vs. passive viewing) rather than cue versus neutral/control stimuli. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 and cannot be included in a meta-analysis requiring reward-cue > control stimulus contrasts. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual Pavlovian cues (colored lights and snack images) associated with food rewards (natural rewards). The study includes within-subject contrasts comparing cue types (e.g., CS+ > CS− and specific PIT contrasts) that reflect cue-evoked activation, reports whole-brain group-level analyses (with results and a NeuroVault collection of maps), and provides participant demographics, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps/results.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual stimuli (images of palatable foods) to probe natural reward-related cue-reactivity in adolescents. The design includes within-participant contrasts (palatable vs non-palatable and palatable vs neutral) and group-level, whole-brain, voxel-wise analyses (ANOVA and second-level mixed-effects models) using SPM8 on a 3.0T scanner. Relevant participant information (age group: adolescents) and cue type (food) are reported. Although some between-group voxel-wise results did not survive multiple-comparison correction and some activation contrasts are not fully reported in the text, whole-brain analyses were performed and described. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts, voxelwise whole-brain group analyses (flexible factorial Time x Stimulation interaction and one-sample t-test for smoking>neutral) with cluster-level correction and reported significant clusters (tables/figures). Methods state MRI field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM12); participant age range and sex/gender comparisons are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of amphetamine-related cue reactivity using visual stimuli (drug-related films). It reports a within-subject Drug movies > Neutral movies contrast and group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results with FWE correction; processing software (SPM12), scanner field strength (3T), participant age and sex are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of cigarette (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (dynamic videos). It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking > neutral cues, reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (peak coordinates and z-statistics reported), and provides necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, and FSL processing). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli of natural rewards (foods containing chili). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (spicy food > non-spicy food), and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with whole-brain FWE correction. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study of visual drug (cocaine) and natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using backward-masked visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine vs. neutral; sexual vs. neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; statistical parametric t maps, cluster statistics and coordinates). Participant demographics (age, sex) are provided (22 male cocaine patients; mean age ~41), cue types (cocaine and sexual), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward). It reports within-subject contrasts of high-hedonic food cues > control stimuli (H > U and U > O) and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with correction for multiple comparisons. Relevant participant details (age range, sex distribution), cue type (food), scanner field (3.0 T), and processing software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This study is not an fMRI study and does not report any task-evoked whole-brain fMRI activation maps. It is an interventional tDCS study with behavioral and cognitive/subjective measures (appetite VAS, n-back task) in participants with obesity; no MRI data, no within-participant fMRI contrast of food cues>control, and no voxelwise whole-brain results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (functional MRI study) and related requirements (I4, I5). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual chocolate pictures vs neutral pictures, with within-subject contrasts (chocolate>neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise regression analyses reported. The paper reports whole-brain results (cluster-corrected) with anatomical localisation and cluster coordinates, and provides participant sex (female undergraduates), cue type (food/chocolate), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue processing using visual stimuli and reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results with scanner and processing details, the reported fMRI analyses focus on contrasts between cognitive reappraisal instructions and an 'imagine eating' instruction for appetizing foods. The paper does not report a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., appetizing food > unappetizing food or food images > neutral/non-food images) in the provided full text. Because the meta-analysis requires at least one cue>control within-subject contrast, this study does not meet inclusion criterion I4 and thus must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (e-cigarette) cue-reactivity that used visual stimuli (images of e-cigarettes) and within-subject contrasts (sweet-, nicotine-, and sweet+nicotine-paired cues versus control). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (including exploratory whole-brain results and correlations that survived whole-brain correction) and also small-volume ROI tests; methods report participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine/e-cigarette), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM12). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (food video epochs > control video epochs). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM2 with family-wise error correction and reporting of activation clusters (coordinates referenced in Table 2). Relevant participant details (sex, age range), cue type (food), MRI field strength (4T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are violated.

The study does not address the review objective of fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. It uses a monetary reward prediction task (colored circles predicting monetary gains/losses), not drug cues or the natural reward cue types specified (nicotine visual cues would count only if they were smoking images; money is not among included cue types). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrasts of drug cues>control or natural reward cues>control). The full text is complete and the paper does report whole-brain analyses and scanner/processing details (satisfying I5 and I7), but failure to meet I3/I4 excludes it from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual presentation (participants viewed/held a cigarette via live video feed). The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing cigarette versus control cues (paired t-test and regression analyses of cigarette>control), and uses whole-brain, voxelwise group-level GLM analyses with cluster-correction (AFNI/FSL reported). Scanner field strength (3-Tesla) and processing software are specified; participant sex is reported (n female = 12) and demographic variables are described. Results are reported in the text with anatomical loci and cluster statistics (coordinates/figures/tables referenced). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) in adolescents. The task includes within-subject contrasts of appetizing versus plain food (appetizing vs. plain > baseline) at first-level and reports one-sample (within-group) and two-sample (between-group) whole-brain voxelwise analyses with appropriate multiple-comparison correction. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T) and processing software (SPM8). Results are reported at the group level with whole-brain statistics and correlations with behavioral craving measures. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps/results.

This is an fMRI study of food cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts and a reported exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analysis; however the manuscript as provided does not report MRI scanner field strength (e.g., 1.5T or 3T), which is required by inclusion criterion I7. Therefore not all required inclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete otherwise.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward stimuli (romantic/sexual images) and assesses cue-reactivity (romantic vs. neutral). Within-subject contrasts (Romantic > Neutral) were conducted, and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed using SPM8 with cluster correction. Methods report participant age and sex (female, 18–25), cue type (romantic/sexual), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking-related pictures (drug cues) and matched neutral images. It includes within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral), and reports a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise 2x2 ANOVA with clusterwise FWE-corrected results and ROIs derived from those whole-brain maps. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI, FSL) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of sexual (natural reward) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (video clips). The task includes within-subject contrasts of sexual cues versus control (explicit > exciting and erotic > exciting). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain FWE-corrected activations for explicit–exciting and other contrasts across groups and between-group comparisons), and coordinates/tables/figures and supplementary tables are referenced. Participant age and sex and cue type are clearly reported; processing software (SPM8) is specified. While scanner acquisition parameters/field strength are referenced rather than spelled out in the excerpt (“acquisition parameters of the fMRI study are described in .”), the full text includes methods and whole-brain results typical of PLoS ONE articles, and the necessary voxelwise task maps are presented. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI visual-cue reactivity studies of natural rewards.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts of hedonic food > non-food objects, and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM5 with thresholding and reported activation coordinates. Scanner field strength (3.0 T), processing software (SPM5), participant ages and sex, and cue type (food) are all reported. The manuscript contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are violated. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual food cue-reactivity (natural reward). The primary within-subject contrast examined high-caloric > low-caloric food cues (HC vs LC) and reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results using SPM12 with cluster FWE correction and reported cluster coordinates. Participant age and sex (20 healthy males, mean age 24.9) are reported, cue type is food, MRI field strength is 3T, and preprocessing/analysis software (SPM12) is specified. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food). It includes within-subject contrasts of hedonic food images > neutral control images (H>O), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM5 with FDR correction, and presents task-evoked statistical maps/coordinates and figures. Relevant participant information (age range, sex breakdown), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using visual methamphetamine-related cues in a sample of 26 methamphetamine-dependent participants and 26 controls. The design includes within-subject task contrasts (methamphetamine-cue task versus rest baseline) and group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM5 with a voxelwise threshold and cluster extent—i.e., whole-brain, group-level task activation maps. The manuscript reports participant age and sex, cue type (methamphetamine), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5). The full-text contains background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for visual drug-cue fMRI whole-brain task activation contrasts and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and reports within-participant contrasts of food cues > control (fattening and nonfattening food vs objects) pre- and postmeal. The paper reports both ROI and voxel-wise exploratory whole-brain analyses (cluster-thresholded Z statistic images, voxel-wise exploratory analyses outside ROIs with a Z threshold), and describes whole-brain anatomic locations and coordinates in text/figures/supplement. Participant age range and sex composition are reported, and cue type is food. Imaging acquisition/processing methods are referenced and likely detailed in the supplemental methods; whole-brain results are described in the main text and figures. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity with whole-brain task-evoked results. I note minor uncertainty because specific scanner field strength and processing software are not explicitly shown in the provided excerpt but are referenced as described elsewhere (supplement), so confidence is 0.80.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject Food > Non-Food contrasts, participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). However, the published analyses are focused on ROI-based extraction and a balance score; the manuscript does not report or present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or coordinate table/figure of whole-brain Food>Control results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked evidence and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

This publication is a study protocol (no original empirical fMRI results or group-level whole-brain activation maps are reported). Although the planned methods describe fMRI cue-reactivity to visual smoking and food cues (and relevant scanner and processing details), the paper does not present any task-evoked, whole-brain statistical maps or empirical contrasts (drug cue > control) required for inclusion. Therefore it qualifies as a non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data and should be excluded under E6.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and an explicit within-participant contrast of food cues versus control (nature) images. The authors generated subject-level whole-brain contrast images and submitted them to a second-level group T-map (group-level, voxelwise task activation). Key methodological details are reported (participant age and sex, cue type: food, scanner field strength: 3-T Philips Intera Achieva, and processing software: SPM8). Reporting of whole-brain results is described and acceptable (group T-map and follow-up ROI analyses). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The methods describe within-participant contrasts of high-energy-dense (high-ED) vs. low-ED food cues (a valid cue>control-type contrast for reward reactivity), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM8; cluster-corrected maps and thresholding described). Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software are reported. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual cues as defined for the meta-analysis. It examines neural responses to smoking-cessation messages (persuasive/educational stimuli) rather than cue-reactivity to smoking-related cues intended to elicit craving/approach (e.g., pictures/videos of cigarettes or other drug cues). Although the study includes within-participant contrasts (smoking-cessation messages > neutral), reports voxel-wise exploratory whole-brain results (coordinate tables/clusters), and provides participant demographics, it fails inclusion criterion I3 (cue-reactivity stimulus type) required by the review. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in a within-subject design, the full text reports only seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity analyses. The paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map (e.g., food>control contrast) within this manuscript (it references a prior BOLD analysis in a separate publication). Per the review criteria, studies reporting only seed-based/effective connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map must be excluded (E4). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > control). However, all reported task-evoked group analyses were conducted within an ROI mask with small-volume correction (SVC); no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level activation maps are reported. The meta-analysis requires at least one whole-brain task-evoked map. Because the study reports only ROI-based whole-brain-masked results and not an unmasked whole-brain activation map, it meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) and examines cue-reactivity. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing high-calorie food cues to low-calorie/control stimuli (e.g., high-calorie go > low-calorie go; nogo vs go contrasts) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, Z>2.3 cluster-corrected) using FSL on a 3T scanner. Participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength, and processing software are all reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual natural reward-related cues (food) that reports within-participant contrasts (high-energy vs. neutral; low-energy vs. neutral; high vs. low) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise thresholds (whole-brain FDR P<0.05 and cluster thresholds; interaction effects with P<0.005 reported). Methods report cue type (food), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM12); participant sex (female/college-age sample) and BMI range are provided. Whole-brain activation results are described in the text (regions/clusters). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (natural rewards) presented with a backward-masking paradigm. It reports within-subject contrasts of sexual cues versus neutral and fixation (Sex vs Neu; Sex vs Fix) and includes group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-test for task effects thresholded and cluster-corrected). Results are reported with significant clusters/coordinates. Participant age and sex (young healthy males), cue type (sexual), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (FSL) are all provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of Sexual versus Neutral outcomes and cues, and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain cluster FWE-corrected maps with coordinates reported). Relevant metadata are provided (male participants, age group described as young/’comparably aged’, cue type sexual, 3T scanner, SPM8 processing). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of visual natural reward cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual stimuli (advertisements/images) to measure cue-reactivity to a nicotine-related product (e-cigarettes) in young adults. Within-participant contrasts comparing flavored/tobacco e-cigarette cues versus control images are reported. The paper includes group-level whole-brain task activation results (exploratory whole-brain analyses reported with FWE cluster correction and cluster-forming threshold), and provides relevant participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cues using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts (e.g., Food vs Objects, Unhealthy vs Objects) and group-level random-effects analyses including whole-brain results. However, the full text as provided does not report MRI scanner field strength, which is required by inclusion criterion I7 (relevant information regarding participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). Because not all inclusion criteria are verifiably met (I7 missing), the study must be excluded.

This study does not meet the review's key inclusion requirement that cue-reactivity be assessed using visual stimuli (I3). The experimental manipulation used gustatory (taste) high-calorie cues delivered in the scanner (high-calorie drinks vs. water); although brief visual instructions accompanied delivery, the primary reward cues were tastes rather than visual stimuli. The study does satisfy several other inclusion criteria (within-subject contrast of high-calorie cues > control (water) (I4), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (I5), and reporting of whole-brain results in text/figures (I6)). Some required participant details are incomplete in the provided full text: age range is reported but sex distribution is not clearly provided in the excerpt, raising uncertainty about I7. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not use visual cue stimuli as required by the meta-analysis objective.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (explicit sexual images). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing sexual versus neutral pictures (Sex LO > Neutral LO; Sex PC > Neutral PC). Group-level second-level analyses were performed and the paper indicates whole-brain analyses are available in the supplementary material (coordinates/whole-brain results described). Participant age and sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. Although ROI analyses are emphasized, whole-brain results are reported/available, so the study does not meet exclusion for ROI-only reporting. Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

While this is an fMRI study using visual drug-related cues and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps (FSL/SPM, 3T scanner) and participant info, it does not present a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control (or natural reward > control) that represents standard cue-reactivity. The primary reported contrasts evaluate premature>correct responses within incentive contexts and interactions between premature responses across money vs drug conditions, rather than a simple drug‑cue > neutral cue contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met, so the study cannot be included in a meta-analysis of cue‑reactivity contrasts.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual cues (pornographic pictures) to test cue-reactivity and their effect on task performance. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of explicit (pornographic) > neutral pictures and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM12) with whole-brain cluster-level FWE correction, and provides peak activations/tables and figures. Relevant participant information (male, age means), cue type (sexual), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. The explicitness (pornographic>neutral) main effect and interaction contrasts constitute appropriate task-evoked whole-brain maps matching the meta-analysis objective of natural reward (sexual) visual cue-reactivity.

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual stimuli (I3 satisfied), the published analyses in this full text use an ROI approach and report ROI-based contrasts (e.g., Large PS > Small PS) rather than presenting group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. The paper explicitly states the present study used an ROI approach and does not report whole-brain results for the contrasts relevant to cue-reactivity. Therefore it violates the review's requirement for whole-brain evidence and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported).

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual stimuli and reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses, the group-level results presented are exclusively pre-post (surgery) difference maps (nogo_dessert_pre - nogo_dessert_post, nogo_vegetable_pre - nogo_vegetable_post). The study does not report an accompanying unmasked, group-level cue>control (e.g., food cues > control stimuli or food > neutral) whole-brain task activation map. The meta-analysis requires at least one within-participant cue>control group-level whole-brain map; reporting only time/difference contrasts without the main task effect meets exclusion criterion E5. Subject-level cue>rest contrasts were computed but not provided at the group level as the required cue>control effect for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues (pictures) and neutral/evocative controls (meets cue modality). It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking vs. neutral) with observed increases in NAcc and amygdala activation in smokers. Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with cluster-correction and small-volume corrections; results are reported in text/tables and ROI analyses. Methods report participant demographics (age/gender distribution summarized), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0T) and processing software (AFNI). Therefore all required inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity whole-brain fMRI studies are satisfied.

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts (hedonic > neutral foods; foods > non-food objects) and reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8), the study used an ROI-based analysis approach and explicitly notes that sample size was insufficient for whole-brain analysis. No unmasked, group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain coordinate tables/figures are reported for the primary contrasts. This violates the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

The article is an fMRI event-related cue reactivity study using visual drug and food stimuli with within-subject contrasts (drug>neutral, food>neutral) and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses and AFNI preprocessing. Participant age and sex are reported. However, the full text provided does not report the MRI scanner field strength (e.g., 1.5T or 3T) in the main text; while supplementary materials are referenced, they were not provided here. Inclusion criterion I7 requires reporting of scanner field strength along with other methodological details. Because that required piece of information is not available in the provided full text, the study does not meet all inclusion criteria and must be excluded from the meta-analysis based on the information given.

Although this is an fMRI study that used visual cues to predict a natural reward (juice), the reported task analyses are based on region-of-interest (caudate and putamen) extracted activity measures and GWAS of those ROI values. The paper does not report a within-participant cue>control (or cue>neutral) contrast in the form needed for cue-reactivity meta-analysis, nor does it present group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinate tables of whole-brain task effects. Therefore it fails the required whole-brain task-evoked evidence and effectively reports only ROI-based task results. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing cigarette-predictive cues (CS+) versus control cues (CS−) (e.g., Attend CS+ vs Attend CS−) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (statistical maps reported at p<0.001). Participant age and sex (all male, ages reported), cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5 and FSL) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual monetary reward cues (ring of dollar signs) and neutral cues, with within-subject contrasts of reward vs. neutral trials. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (linear mixed effects on IRFs, cluster correction via AlphaSim) with reported peak coordinates and time courses. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (monetary reward), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (FSL, AFNI) are reported. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for natural reward cue-reactivity and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (package images) and within-participant contrasts comparing package types (regular vs healthier) and package/taste conditions. The study reports group-level voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain analyses followed by ROI masking) and provides cluster results and correlations; participant age/sex (34 healthy females, ages reported), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. Reporting includes whole-brain results (clusters/thresholds) and coordinates in text/supplement. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of food cue reactivity using visual stimuli with whole-brain analyses and appropriate reporting (age/sex, cue type = food, 3T scanner, SPM8). However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of food cues versus a non-food control (neutral) stimulus; all experimental conditions are food images (high vs low calorie, available vs unavailable). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 (no cue>control stimulus contrast). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) directly apply.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (food images) with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie vs. nonfood object; low-calorie vs. nonfood object) during premeal and postmeal states. Group-level voxelwise GLM results are reported, with whole-brain thresholds (p<.001, cluster >5, FDR corrected) and region-level results/coordinates and activation maps described in the text/figures. Cue type (food), MRI field strength (4.0T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. Participant sample size and BMI groupings are provided; a participant characteristics table is referenced (suggesting age/sex were reported in the full article). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 for the meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI study of monetary incentive delay task using visual object cues and monetary gain/loss anticipation; it does not investigate cue-reactivity to drug cues (e.g., nicotine, alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, heroin) or natural reward-related cues specified by the review (e.g., food, sexual). Therefore it fails the key inclusion criterion I3. The manuscript does include within-participant contrasts (gain>neutral, loss>neutral) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results, coordinate tables/figures, participant age/sex, cue type (monetary), scanner (3T) and processing software (SPM8), so I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (written labels and cue images). The authors report within-subject contrasts comparing labeled beverage cues (low-calorie, high-calorie, neutral) including high>low, low>high, and comparisons versus neutral. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (SPM8) with cluster-level FWE correction reported; details on participants (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical within-subject, double-blind placebo-controlled fMRI study using visual erotic (sexual) scenes as natural reward cues and neutral control stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (erotic > neutral, fearful > neutral, erotic > fearful) and group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected results (and supplementary uncorrected maps), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant age and sex (55 healthy young males, mean age reported), cue type (sexual/erotic), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with group-level, whole-brain task analyses and adequate reporting of participants, scanner, and processing (satisfying I3, I5, I6, I7), it lacks a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control (neutral) stimuli as required by I4. The reported contrasts compare food images with and without calorie labels (CALORIES vs NO CALORIES) rather than food cues versus a neutral/non-reward control condition. No unmasked whole-brain cue>control contrast is described, so the study does not meet the essential I4 inclusion criterion for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

Although the article examines neural responses related to food cues and reports behavioral craving ratings to visual food stimuli, the fMRI data are resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses (no task fMRI cue-reactivity scan). There is no within-participant task contrast of food cues > control stimuli and no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported. Therefore the study does not meet I3, I4, or I5 and directly meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only seed-based/resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (food > non-food; high-calorie > low-calorie). The authors report group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise) with cluster-correction and describe significant clusters, and also provide ROI analyses. Relevant methodological details are reported: participant age range, mention of sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual cues (natural reward) and neutral controls. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing sexual > neutral backgrounds (task-based cue-reactivity), performed whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses using SPM12 with FDR-corrected results and reported activation tables/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software are all reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (penile-vaginal penetration) relevant to natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity. The manuscript reports within-subject contrasts of sexual cues versus control stimuli (e.g., PEN>BOD, PEN>NEU). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM8; FWE-corrected maps and conjunction analyses; figures of whole-brain results are provided). Relevant participant and scanner details are reported (female participants with ages, 3T Philips scanner, SPM8 preprocessing). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI study using visual erotic pictures (sexual natural rewards) in a within-subject, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., placebo erotic > placebo neutral; GHB neutral > placebo neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain threshold p<.001 reported), with ROI analyses supplementary. Participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports task activation maps).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of food cues > nonfood control stimuli, reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked analyses (whole-brain results described and illustrated), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM-12). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study (visual alcohol cues) with 61 adult nondependent drinkers. It includes a within-participant contrast of alcohol versus neutral cues, reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (voxel p<.001 with cluster p<.05 FWE) with coordinates/clusters provided, and reports processing software (SPM). Participant sex and cue type are described; imaging protocol details are available in the supplementary material. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity whole-brain fMRI studies and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (food) in human participants. It presents within-subject contrasts of food>control (HC–C, LC–C, HC–LC, Food–C) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with cluster-wise inference and reported clusters/coordinates. Relevant participant and imaging details are reported (female participants with PCOS, scanner 3.0T Siemens, processing with SPM8; cue type = food). Results include whole-brain task-evoked maps and covariate analyses (insulin sensitivity, BMI).
