No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so is complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues and within-subject contrasts of high-calorie versus low-calorie foods, and reports participant details; however, the reported analyses are ROI-based (parameter estimates extracted from a priori ROIs) with no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or coordinate tables presented in the full text. Inclusion requires at least one whole-brain, group-level task activation map (voxelwise) or clearly described whole-brain results. Therefore the study must be excluded (E3).

This study investigates maternal neural responses to infant faces and cries (social/parental cues), not drug cues or the natural reward types targeted in the review (e.g., food or sexual cues). It therefore does not satisfy key inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli of the specified types) or I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli). The full text is complete and does report whole-brain voxelwise analyses (satisfying I5), reports whole-brain results in the text/tables (I6), and provides participant/scanner/processing details (I7). Because I3 and I4 are not met, the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study of food (natural reward) cues meets multiple inclusion criteria: it uses visual food stimuli (I3), reports within-participant contrasts (highly desirable>less desirable; food>non-food) (I4), and reports group-level second-level voxelwise statistics with coordinate-level results and SVC-corrected peaks (I5,I6). However, it does not report essential participant age information or explicitly state the primary processing software used (only indirect mention of marsbar), so it fails inclusion criterion I7 requiring relevant info on participant age, sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an fMRI investigation of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-participant contrasts (fattening food > object, non-fattening > object). It reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). However, group-level analyses were conducted using a region-of-interest (14 predefined ROIs) approach with cluster-thresholding within ROIs; the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group task-evoked statistical map. Because the study reports only ROI-based group analyses and no whole-brain group activation map, it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of sexual (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual pornographic stimuli with within-subject pornographic>neutral contrasts and group-level whole-brain analyses (SPM12). Participant age and sex are reported. However, the manuscript does not report MRI scanner field strength (fMRI acquisition section refers to another source: 'See .'), so it fails inclusion criterion I7 requiring relevant reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. All other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met. Because I7 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded per the review rules (any unmet inclusion criterion leads to exclusion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (food vs. non-food and food vs. blurry baseline) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (t-tests and ANOVA) with cluster-corrected thresholds; coordinates and Talairach/BA locations are provided for key effects. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual monetary incentive cues (rings of $ vs #) and reports within-subject contrasts of reward>neutral (natural reward-related cues vs control). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were performed (AFNI 3dLME) with cluster-level correction and reported statistical maps/ROIs. Participant age and sex, cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (FSL, AFNI) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-subject task effects).

Although this is an fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (food) with clearly reported participants, scanner (3T), stimuli, and SPM2 processing, the analyses are reported using an a priori ROI approach with small-volume correction within defined ROIs. The paper does not present unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps; results are confined to ROIs and SVC-corrected clusters. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual nicotine cues and within-subject task conditions (smoke, neutral, rest), the provided full text reports individualized ROI selection and ROI-based neurofeedback analyses (percent signal change within subject-tailored vACC/dmPFC ROIs) and group-level t-tests on these ROIs. The manuscript does not present or describe an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinate table of whole-brain smoke>neutral activation. Therefore it reports only ROI-based results without qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results, meeting exclusion criterion E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with event-related presentation of food vs visually matched non-food images. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food>non-food, whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (FEAT/FSL) with cluster correction and tables/figures of activations, and provides participant age range/sex information, cue type (food), scanner field strength (Philips 3T), and processing software (FSL). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual cues with within-subject contrasts (HC–control, LC–control) and adequate reporting of participants, scanner (3T), and processing (SPM8), the reported analyses and results are presented as ROI-based/small-volume-corrected activations rather than unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps. The manuscript describes a second-level repeated measures ANOVA but applies an a priori ROI analysis (masks and small-volume correction) and reports ROI activations; there is no clear presentation of unmasked whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain corrected results. Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only results) and does not satisfy the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task activation map (I5). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that presented visual food stimuli (also auditory) and analyzed within-subject contrasts (high- vs low-calorie foods and food vs non-food). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 with cluster-correction and reported task-evoked statistical maps/clusters (with thresholds and cluster extent determined by AlphaSim), satisfying whole-brain reporting standards. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural (sexual/social) reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (male/female faces). It reports within-participant contrasts related to reward cues versus control stimuli (anticipation of smiling faces vs dysmorphed control images) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain results for main effects and exploratory whole-brain results with coordinates). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (sexual/face stimuli), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using audio/visual (visual) stimuli and includes within-participant contrasts of smoking cues versus matched non-smoking cues. However, all reported group-level analyses were conducted within an a priori ROI mask (ventral medial PFC, ventral striatum/pallidum, insula, hippocampus, amygdala, and dorsal striatum added retrospectively). The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map at the group level; results are limited to ROI-based inference. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. The study reports within-participant contrasts of food>object (food vs. matched object images) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected permutation tests) as well as ROI analyses. Relevant details are provided: participant age and sex, cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (FSL). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual-cue reward fMRI studies.

This study reports development and behavioral validation of visual cue pictures and an fMRI paradigm but did not acquire or analyze any fMRI data. It reports self-reported VAS craving only and no within-participant fMRI contrast of drug-cue > control, no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate results. Therefore it does not meet the core inclusion requirements for neuroimaging studies (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). It is a methods/behavioral validation paper without original human fMRI results, so it must be excluded from a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs. non-alcohol beverage pictures) in adolescents. It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol>non-alcohol) and conducts both ROI and exploratory whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (3dttest++ with cluster correction), with results described in the text for whole-brain clusters. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue reactivity using visual smoking images and within-subject smoking>nonsmoking contrasts, and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, all reported task analyses focus on ROI-based parameter estimates and targeted ROI/mediation models; the manuscript does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain coordinates/figures of an unmasked task effect. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli, with a within-subject food > nonfood contrast and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported. The manuscript provides participant demographics (age, sex distribution implied), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). Whole-brain statistical maps (F, t, r) and cluster-level correction procedures are described; results are reported across the brain and referenced to anatomical labels, fulfilling acceptable reporting via text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are violated.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts comparing food pictures versus neutral objects. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (RFX ANOVA F-maps and conjunction t-maps) are reported, with thresholding and Talairach coordinates for identified fROIs. Relevant participant information (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and reports participant demographics and scanner/processing details (meets I3 and I7). However, it does not report a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control (no food>neutral or food>non-food contrast); instead contrasts Enhance vs Regulate (both conditions use palatable food images), so I4 is not met. Additionally, group analyses were performed using ROI-based small-volume correction without reporting unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps; thus the study effectively reports only ROI-corrected results, triggering exclusion under E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts of food > scenery. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (t maps, peak coordinates, cluster thresholds), and results are described in text, tables, and figures. Participant age/sex (healthy adult males), cue type (food), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software (fmristat) are provided. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of food cue reactivity using personalized guided-imagery (auditory) scripts rather than visual stimuli. The review’s I3 requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, which is not met. The study does meet several other inclusion criteria (within-subject contrasts of favorite-food cue > neutral, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected maps and coordinates reported, and relevant participant/cue/scanner information), but failure to use visual cues is sufficient to exclude it from this meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cost–benefit decision making using a Cigarette Purchase Task (economic choices about purchasing cigarettes), not a cue-reactivity paradigm presenting visual drug- or reward-related cues. It does not include within-participant contrasts of drug-cue > control-stimuli or natural-reward-cue > control-stimuli. The paper does report group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and provides participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength and processing software, so it meets I5, I6, and I7, but it fails to meet key inclusion criteria I3 and I4. Therefore it must be excluded from this meta-analysis focused on visual cue-reactivity.

The article does not report task-based fMRI cue-reactivity using visual drug or natural-reward cues. The neuroimaging reported is resting-state fMRI and diffusion tensor imaging (structural) in relation to mindfulness training; behavioral measures (craving, smoking) are reported but there are no within-subject contrasts of drug-cue > control-stimuli or whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Thus it fails to meet inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5 and matches exclusion criterion E4 (resting-state/structural analyses without a whole-brain task activation map).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (food) using visual stimuli (food words). It includes within-subject contrasts of food>neutral (food-fneu) at the group level, reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and statistical thresholds, and provides participant demographics (age, sex distribution), cue type (food words), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Results are reported as whole-brain effects and coordinates in the text/tables, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and a within-participant contrast (alcohol > pleasant). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (activation in left caudate and occipital cortex) with coordinates and cluster sizes described in the text and refers to supplemental materials for full acquisition and preprocessing details. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is alcohol, and scanner/acquisition/processing details are indicated to be available in the Supplement. The study therefore satisfies the review’s requirements for an fMRI drug-cue visual stimulus task, a within-subject drug>control contrast, whole-brain results reported in the text/tables, and reporting of participant and methodological details (with additional scanner/software details provided in supplement). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains whole-brain within-subject effects, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food pictures) with within-participant contrasts of food vs non-food stimuli, and group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (random-effects, voxelwise maps) identifying brain regions responsive to food cues. Participant age and sex and cue type are reported; MRI acquisition and preprocessing details are indicated to be provided in the supplementary material, satisfying reporting requirements. The study thus meets the meta-analysis objective (visual reward cue-reactivity) and all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task activation maps, is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of a natural reward (food) using visual cues (milkshake image vs water) and tastes. It reports within-participant contrasts of milkshake cues > control (milkshake picture > water picture) and milkshake taste > tasteless, and conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using FSL with cluster-based correction. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are all reported. Results are presented as whole-brain clusters described in the text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject contrast of high-calorie > low-calorie food images. The methods report fMRI acquisition (3T) and processing (SPM8) and participant age/sex characteristics. Although the primary reported effect is in the hypothalamus using an ROI and small-volume correction, the authors explicitly state they carried out an exploratory whole-brain (voxelwise) analysis (at p<0.05 FWE) and report the outcome (no other regional differences). Thus a group-level whole-brain task analysis was performed and reported in the text. All required information (cue type, scanner field strength, software) is provided and the full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Given these elements, the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual natural reward cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts relevant to cue-reactivity (e.g., healthy-food-choice > healthy-food-reject, and Tasty-Diet (TD) > No-Diet (ND) conditions), conducted at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8). Coordinates and cluster results are reported and scanner parameters (3T), participant age/sex/BMI, cue type (food), and processing software are provided. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity with whole-brain results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (a natural reward). It contains within-subject contrasts of food > nonfood, reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with corrected cluster results and coordinates, and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with a within-participant contrast of palatable food > neutral items. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (FWE-corrected effects, Talairach/MNI coordinates reported), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The paper reports participant age range (adolescents/young adults), mentions sex comparisons, cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3.0T) and processing software (SPM8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of high-calorie vs. non-food images (pre- and post-meal), and presents group-level whole-brain, voxelwise statistical maps with cluster-based correction and Talairach coordinates. Relevant metadata are provided (participant age and sex, cue type = food, scanner field strength = 3.0 T, processing software = BrainVoyager). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (food pictures) vs nonfood control (animals) to assess reward-related cue reactivity in overweight adolescent girls. The study reports within-participant contrasts (food > nonfood) and conducts group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses with cluster-level correction. Key methodological details required by the review are reported: participant age and sex (15–20 y, female), cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3-Tesla Siemens Trio), and processing software (Brain Voyager QX). Full article text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI investigation of response inhibition using abstract visual stimuli (geometric shapes) in methamphetamine-dependent and control participants. It does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity (no drug/food/sexual cues), nor does it include a within-subject contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural-reward cues > control stimuli. Thus it fails inclusion criteria I3 and I4. The full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, and discussion).

This is a human fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of cocaine/paraphernalia). It includes a within-subject contrast of cocaine pictures > neutral objects and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM8 with cluster-level correction, with results described in the text (activation in putamen, insula, occipital cortex) and supplemental figures. Relevant participant information (age range 18–65, men and women), cue type (cocaine), MRI field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an adult fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts of alcohol vs. neutral cues. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t-test of alcohol>neutral, whole-brain regression vs. SCR) with peak coordinates and cluster statistics described. Participant demographics (age used as covariate, sex counts reported), cue type (alcohol), and processing software (SPM) are specified; scanner details are likely in the Supplement (acceptable per inclusion criteria). The study therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue fMRI whole-brain task activation maps and reports necessary methodological details.

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (beer images) in a Go/NoGo task comparing responses to alcohol vs non-alcohol stimuli. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (thresholded whole-brain maps) and presents activation maps for NoGo (beer) trials and between-group contrasts (heavy > light) with whole-brain inference. Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. Individual subject-level contrasts for Go and NoGo conditions were created and entered into second-level analyses, providing the within-participant condition contrasts needed for cue>control comparisons. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues with within-participant food>non-food contrasts and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, the manuscript reports results derived from region-of-interest (ROI) percent signal-change extractions and does not present or describe group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, coordinates, or cluster tables in the provided full text. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results).

Although this is an empirical fMRI study in cocaine-dependent individuals that includes cue exposure for behavioral craving measures, the MRI analyses do not report a within-participant visual cue-reactivity contrast (drug cues > control stimuli). The reported whole-brain voxelwise maps are TMS-evoked BOLD responses and pre/post cTBS (real vs sham) effects, not task-based cue-reactivity to visual drug cues. Therefore criteria I3 and I4 (fMRI of visual cue-reactivity and a within-subject cue>control contrast) are not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present) but no qualifying cue-reactivity fMRI maps are described. Exclusion from the meta-analysis is warranted.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (viewing food > viewing non-food; distraction food > distraction non-food). Analyses are group-level whole-brain voxelwise using SPM8 with reported cluster coordinates and thresholding (FWE cluster-corrected), and the paper reports participant sex/age, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures/videos and written visual cues). It includes within-subject contrasts CUE SEM > CUE NEUTRAL and SEM > NEUTRAL, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected clusters and coordinates), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of monetary reward anticipation using the Monetary Incentive Delay task (visual cues for £5, £1, £0). Although it includes within-participant reward>neutral contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates, and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM8), it does not assess drug-related cues or natural reward-related cues (e.g., food, sexual) as defined by the review objective. Monetary reward cues do not meet the meta-analysis’s specified domain of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3.

This is an empirical fMRI study employing visual alcohol cues (alcohol-related images) and neutral images in an alcohol cue reactivity (ACR) task. It reports within-subject alcohol>neutral contrasts (GLM, one-sample t-tests) and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation results (alcohol > neutral) with voxelwise and cluster-level correction. Participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio) and detailed acquisition parameters are reported; preprocessing is referenced and reported in Supplementary Methods (fulfilling reporting requirements). The study therefore satisfies all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cue-induced desire for Internet video game play using visual stimuli. It includes a within-subject contrast (video-game cue > neutral control), reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects results with coordinates and cluster statistics (FDR-corrected), and provides participant age/sex information, scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). Although the cue type is Internet video game (a behavioral/non-drug reward), the review objective includes drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity; gaming can be considered a non-drug reward cue within that scope. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the inclusion criteria for whole-brain task-evoked cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

The reported fMRI results in this full text focus on emotional face processing (faces vs shapes) and oxytocin modulation, not on drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity contrasts. Although an alcohol cue-reactivity task was performed, its results are reported in a parent study and are not presented here. Therefore the paper does not provide a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast nor a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map of drug or natural reward cue-reactivity required for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking > control). However, the voxelwise second-level analyses were conducted within anatomically defined ROI masks (Harvard-Oxford atlases) and results are presented as ROI-based activations/deactivations. There is no evidence in the full text that an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map was performed or reported. Therefore the study reports only ROI-restricted task results and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). The full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in heavy drinkers using visual cues (images) of alcohol and food (natural reward). The AFID task included within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs neutral and alcohol vs food) and the manuscript reports group-level, voxel-wise whole-brain analyses (linear mixed-effects voxel-wise analyses across the entire brain) with thresholding and cluster correction. Relevant methodological details are reported (participant age/sex information, cue types: alcohol and food, MRI scanner field strength 3T, and processing software AFNI). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided content appears complete for screening. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) and body-image stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of food>control (food vs low-level baseline and food vs non-food), and body>control contrasts. The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (median activation maps, permutation testing, cluster-level inference) with peak Talairach coordinates (e.g., right insula) reported in the text/tables. Relevant participant information (adult female participants), cue type (food, body), MRI field strength (1.5T) and processing software (XBAM) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of visual natural rewards (erotic and monetary) with within-subject contrasts and adequate reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (meets I3, I4, I7). However, the imaging analyses were restricted to predefined region-of-interest (ROI) spheres and reported ROI-based results; no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps are presented or reported (the methods and results emphasize ROI analyses). Therefore the study does not provide whole-brain evidence required by I5 and thus meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This paper includes original fMRI data (case study #2) using visual food cues (natural reward). The methods describe presentation of 180 images (120 food, 30 furniture, 30 scrambled), contrasts (high-ED vs low-ED; food vs non-food), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI preprocessing, 3dMVM ANCOVA, cluster-correction with 3dClustSim) with reported coordinates and cluster statistics. Participant age and sex are reported (7–11-year-old males and females), scanner field strength (3T MAGNETOM Trio), and processing software (AFNI). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in overweight/obese participants. It reports within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood (food vs nonfood images) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected whole-brain correlation maps) as well as ROI results. Relevant participant demographics (age range, sex distribution), cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used visual alcohol cues and reports group-level whole-brain task maps (respond alcohol > rest and respond neutral > rest) and provides demographic, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). However, it does NOT present a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (alcohol cues > neutral/control); authors explicitly state direct comparisons between respond alcohol and respond neutral were not conducted because the task was not structured to allow a clean contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in adolescents. It includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food (HCF) versus nonfood (NF) and low-calorie food (LCF) versus NF, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected; Monte Carlo/AFNI AlphaSim) with regions and effect sizes described in text, figures, and supplementary tables. Key details required by the meta-analysis are reported: participant ages and sex distribution, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (BioImageSuite; AFNI). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports a within-subject contrast comparing conditioned food-related images (CS+) to control images (CS-). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (whole-brain threshold p < .001 uncorrected with reported clusters), and small-volume corrections are also applied; results are reported in text and compared with prior peaks. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI, only-connectivity, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This fMRI study used visual monetary cues (MID task) assessing natural reward-related cue-reactivity (money). It includes within-subject contrasts of Gain Anticipation > Neutral Anticipation, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps (corrected thresholds), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (money), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Full-text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue‑reactivity using visual stimuli (social and non‑social alcohol vs soda images). It includes within‑participant contrasts of alcohol>control (e.g., (SA+NA)>(SS+NS) and interaction contrasts [(SA>SS)-(NA>NS)]), reports group‑level whole‑brain voxelwise analyses with cluster‑level FWE correction, and provides unthresholded T‑maps (NeuroVault). Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue‑reactivity and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of food cues > neutral (HC+LC vs NF), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×3 ANOVA and whole-brain contrasts with FWE correction/AlphaSim), and describes whole-brain contrast maps. Participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM5, AFNI, BioImageSuite) are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task effects, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not assess visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards and does not report a task-evoked whole-brain activation map. Exclusion ID met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity and ALFF analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (participant age/sex, cue type = food, MRI field strength = 3T, and processing software SPM8/Data Processing Assistant are reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (not an fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant contrast of cues>control stimuli), I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain task results in text/figures/tables). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full-text screening indicates the study is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol but used an alcohol taste (gustatory) cue paradigm (Alcohol > Water contrast with taste delivery) rather than a visual cue-reactivity paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant Alcohol>Water contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain task results referenced for ACC/thalamus), I6 (whole-brain results described in text/supplement), and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, software, and scanner details reported/available). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (required use of visual stimuli for cue-reactivity; the primary cue modality here is taste despite brief visual word prompts). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) explicitly apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I3.

Empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). Includes a within-subject contrast of cocaine>neutral cues, with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (FWE-corrected maps, tables/figures provided). Methods report participant demographics (sex; age likely in Table 1), cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This paper is a narrative synthesis/discussion of a series of prior neuroimaging studies rather than an original empirical fMRI report. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical/review paper without original human fMRI data). (b) Inclusion criteria met: none. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an original fMRI study assessing cue-reactivity with visual stimuli), I4 (no reported within-participant drug-cues > control contrast from a primary dataset), I5/I6 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables from a primary analysis are presented for inclusion), I7 (no participant-level details such as age/sex, scanner field strength, or processing software reported as primary study methods). Therefore the article does not meet the meta-analysis requirements.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cocaine-cue videotapes to elicit craving vs baseline/control conditions. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., tape viewing epochs vs baseline; emotion1 vs emotion0) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (randomization procedure, voxelwise p values, figures and a table of regions). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM96) are reported. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study (AUD patients) uses alcohol and food images and reports behavioral cue effects and whole-brain task contrasts for regulation conditions, but it does not report a within-participant whole-brain contrast of drug (alcohol) cues > control stimuli (e.g., alcohol>neutral/food) necessary for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study using visual drug/natural reward cues), I5 (reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps for regulation contrasts), I6 (whole-brain results are clearly described), and I7 (reports participant info, cue types, scanner field strength, and processing software). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no reported within-subject drug-cue > control-stimulus whole-brain contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded from the cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (heroin images) and neutral images. It includes within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral (first-level BOLDdrugcues > BOLDneutral and one-sample/group-level tests) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (whole-brain analyses with cluster-level inference and FWE correction). Relevant methodological details are reported (participant age and sex, cue type: heroin, 3T scanner, processing software SPM8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual natural-reward (food) cue reactivity in pre-pubertal children. It reports within-subject food>non-food contrasts, uses whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (FLAME1; cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<.05), and provides required participant/cue/scanner/processing details (age, sex, food cues, 3T scanner, FSL). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original human fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) and matched neutral images. It reports within-subject Smoking > Neutral contrasts and performs whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FSL/FLAME) with cluster-corrected results. Results are presented in tables and figures, and methods report participant age range/sex composition, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (FSL). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes unmasked whole-brain task effects; empirical data present). Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant cocaine > neutral (control) contrasts and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with voxelwise and cluster thresholds; results are presented as SPM maps and tables/figures. The Methods report cue type (cocaine images), MRI scanner field strength (Siemens 3.0T Trio), processing software (SPM8), and participant sex (5 women, 33 men) and demographic table is referenced. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant task activation maps). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This report is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes a within-subject contrast (Alcohol > Control) entered into group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) GLMs with cluster-level FWE correction and reports MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. Methods state use of a 3-T scanner and SPM12 for processing; participant demographics (age range, sex distribution) and cue type (alcohol visual images) are described. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and is empirical with original human fMRI activation maps). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it used taste/gustatory alcohol and juice cues (in-taste delivery) rather than visual stimuli required by the review. It does meet several other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrast alcohol>juice), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/reported), and I7 (participant age/sex reported, cue type = alcohol, scanner field strength = 3T, processing software = SPM5). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study includes a human fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity experiment with visual stimuli (meets I3), reports within-participant alcohol>neutral cue contrasts in a crossover design (meets I4), and provides group-level whole-brain task activation results (tables/figures reported, meets I5 and I6). However, the provided full text does not report key methodological details required by I7: MRI scanner field strength and fMRI processing software are not specified in the main text excerpt (they may be in Supplementary Information, but only main text was provided and the screening must be based on provided content). Because I7 is not satisfied in the provided full text, the study does not meet ALL inclusion criteria and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply based on the provided content.

This is an fMRI study of reward processing using a monetary incentive delay task (anticipation of monetary reward > verbal feedback). The study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity (no visual drug/food/sexual cue images presented during fMRI), so it does not meet I3 or I4. It does report group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (coordinates and figures) and provides participant age/sex, cue/task type, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8), thus meeting I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDED because inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are not met; inclusion criteria satisfied: I5, I6, I7; inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4; no exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue videos (cocaine, gambling, sad) to elicit drug and gambling cue-reactivity. The design includes within-subject contrasts of video viewing vs baseline (V1>B1 and V2>B2) for cocaine and gambling cues, and reports group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (3×2×3 ANOVA) with FWE correction. Results are presented in tables/figures with coordinates. Participant age and sex, cue types, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5/AFNI/BioImage Suite) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli in treatment-seeking male AUD patients and controls (meets I3). It includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol > neutral stimuli (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (factorial whole-brain analyses, corrected with permutation/cluster thresholds) and provides results in text/tables/figures (meets I5 and I6). Relevant methodological details are reported (participant age and sex, cue type: alcohol, scanner field strength: 3T, processing software: SPM8/SPM12), satisfying I7. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study is a PET imaging study measuring [18F]fallypride displacement (dopamine release) in response to cocaine cues, not an fMRI task activation study. Exclusion reason: E3 applies because the paper reports ROI-based PET analyses and does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues vs neutral control was performed). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an fMRI study), I5 (no whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported), I6 (no whole-brain results reported in coordinates/figures for a task activation), I7 (required fMRI-specific reporting such as MRI scanner field strength and fMRI processing software not provided). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of alcohol and cannabis marketing cue reactivity using visual stimuli (marketing video clips). It reports within-participant contrasts of cannabis marketing > neutral and alcohol marketing > neutral at the first level and group-level GLM whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses using SPM8 on a Siemens 3T scanner. Participant ages and sexes are reported (n=61, 35 men, 26 women, age range 18–28), cue types are alcohol and cannabis, and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM8) and field strength (3T) are stated. Whole-brain results are described in the text, figures, and tables (cluster PFWE-corrected), satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task effects). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related images (I3 met). It includes within-participant contrasts of smoke > rest for ROI selection and PSC analyses (I4 met). Participant demographics, cue type (nicotine), 3T scanner, and processing software (Turbo-BrainVoyager, SPM8) are reported (I7 met). However, the manuscript reports primarily individualized ROI selection and ROI-based percent signal change analyses; no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or corresponding coordinate tables/whole-brain results are reported in the results (only ROI locations and ROI-centers are shown). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Excluding on the basis of E3.

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports only ROI-based neurofeedback analyses (percentage BOLD change in bilateral insula) and behavioral measures; no group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps (drug>neutral) are presented. Inclusion I3 met: this is an fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Inclusion I4 not met: no within-participant drug cues > control stimuli whole-brain contrasts are reported. Inclusion I5 not met: no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map is provided. Inclusion I6 not met (no whole-brain results in tables/figures/text). Inclusion I7 not fully met: while cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (TBV/SPM) are reported, participant age and sex are not clearly reported. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to provide whole-brain task activation results and reports only ROI analyses (E3).

This is an empirical task fMRI study using visual anticipatory cues (shapes in the MID task and faces in the probabilistic reward task) signaling monetary rewards and losses (natural reward-related cues). The study reports within-participant contrasts (Reward Cue–Neutral Cue and Loss Cue–Neutral Cue) and performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported significant clusters (FLAME whole-brain paired t-tests, corrected clusters reported). Reporting includes figures/tables and methodological details required (participant ages and sex, cue type = monetary, 3T MRI scanner, and processing software FSL 5.0.6). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This fMRI study meets several inclusion criteria (I3: visual alcohol cue-reactivity; I4: within-subject alcohol>non-alcohol contrasts; I6: whole-brain results reported in tables/coordinates/figures; I7: reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). However, the second-level group analyses were spatially restricted to an anatomically defined mesocorticolimbic mask rather than an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation map. Thus it does not satisfy I5 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). This violates exclusion criterion E5 (no accompanying unmasked whole-brain task effect). Therefore the study should be excluded.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity that presented visual stimuli (grayscaled images) and haptic stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., VS–VC, HS–HC) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM/ANOVA analyses with cluster-corrected voxelwise results and tables/figures reported. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), MRI scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager) are reported. The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study).

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: cue presentation modality is individualized auditory guided-imagery scripts (audiotaped narratives), not visual stimuli. Met inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrasts: favorite-food/stress vs neutral), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), I7 (reports age/sex, cue type=food, 3T scanner, analysis software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because the meta-analysis specifically requires visual cue-reactivity studies, this auditory-script fMRI study must be excluded.

The full text reports an empirical BOLD fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject CUE>neutral contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FSL FLAME1; voxel-wise correction and cluster-based masks), results are presented in figures and tables, and participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are all described. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without unmasked task effects, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and control (nonalcoholic beverage) images (SSACT). It reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol versus control trials (e.g., CRAlcohol-CRControl), and conducts group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with family-wise error correction, presenting results in tables and figures. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8) are all documented. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task-evoked whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (natural reward). The study reports within-subject contrasts comparing tasty food cues to control stimuli (e.g., ADMIT_TASTY>ADMIT_NOT_TASTY and ADMIT_TASTY>REGULATE_TASTY), and task-evoked group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded voxelwise, FWE cluster correction). Relevant methodological details are reported: participant sex (female), fasting state, use of a 3T scanner, and preprocessing/analysis software (SPM8); participant age is used as a covariate and demographic tables are referenced. Results are presented with whole-brain maps and peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and empirical human fMRI data are provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (palatable food images) with a within-subject contrast (food > nonfood). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholding, MNI coordinates, tables/figures), and whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12/CAT12) are reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of cocaine using visual (audiovisual) stimuli with within-subject cocaine cue > neutral contrasts (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper reports ROI-based analyses focused on a single midcerebellar slice and vermis ROIs rather than a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map; whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables are not provided for a group-level task effect (I5 not met). Processing software is not clearly reported (I7 not met). Because the study reports only ROI analyses without accompanying whole-brain results, it meets exclusion criterion E3. Therefore it must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity but uses gustatory (taste) alcohol cues (alcohol taste vs water) rather than visual stimulus cues. Although brief visual labels (“Alcohol Taste”/“Control Taste”) were presented, the experimental manipulation and primary cues were gustatory, so it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I3 (use of visual stimuli). The study does meet I4 (within-participant Alcohol>Control contrasts), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED because I3 is not met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (films) depicting cocaine use and other content. It reports within-participant contrasts (cocaine film vs nature film; comparisons vs sex film) and group-level voxelwise one-sample and two-sample t tests with whole-brain thresholding and cluster criteria. Whole-brain results are described in text/tables and shown in figures; processing software (AFNI), scanner field strength (1.5 T), participant ages/sex breakdown, and cue type (cocaine) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity with visual drug cues.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (images) in heavy-drinking participants (I3). The authors report within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > rest across training blocks [(alcohol cues − rest) contrasts], including analyses of change over time (I4). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses were conducted and reported (e.g., FWE-corrected results for the right inferior frontal gyrus and reward-localizer effects), with coordinates provided (I5,I6). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3 T) and processing software (SPM8), satisfying reporting requirements (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes whole-brain task-evoked maps (not ROI-only), is not connectivity-only, and reports within-subject task effects. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete / paywalled: only abstract, metadata, and references are available, and explicit methods/results sections are inaccessible. From the abstract, this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using alcohol-related visual video stimuli (satisfies I3) and the authors performed an alcohol vs neutral within-participant contrast (satisfies I4). However, the paper reports that the simple contrast alcohol>neutral was not significant and the main reported findings are psychophysiological interaction (PPI) seed-based connectivity results (seed: posterior cingulate cortex). I cannot verify that a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked (voxelwise) statistical map for alcohol>neutral was reported (I5 not verifiable). Also, key reporting details (participant age/sex, scanner field strength, processing software) are not available in the accessible content (I7 not verifiable). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm all inclusion criteria; therefore the study is excluded pending access to full text for verification.

Full text is not available (site content failed to load); only title/metadata provided. Based on available information, there is no evidence this is an fMRI study or that visual cue-reactivity paradigms were used. Therefore it does not meet the key inclusion criteria: I3 (functional MRI study assessing drug/natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) is not satisfied; I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli) cannot be confirmed; I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map) cannot be confirmed; I7 (reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and processing software) is not available. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confidently applied from the available information. Because the full text is incomplete, exclusion is based on insufficient evidence to meet inclusion criteria. Full text incomplete and core methods/results unavailable.

This study is a functional MRI (CASL perfusion) investigation of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using audiovisual visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > nonsmoking cues). It reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (random-effects), tables of coordinates, and processing software (SPM5). However, the provided full text does not explicitly report the MRI scanner field strength (required per I7). Because inclusion criterion I7 requires reporting participant age and sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software, and scanner field strength is not reported in the provided content, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity using visual videotape stimuli, with within-subject contrasts (cue vs neutral baseline), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster coordinates reported), and participant age/sex and scanner field strength reported. However, the full text does not specify the MRI processing software/package (e.g., SPM, AFNI, FSL) used for preprocessing/statistical analysis, which is required by inclusion criterion I7. All other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting I7.

Although this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cannabis stimuli with within-subject cannabis>neutral contrasts and reports participant demographics and scanner/software (I3, I4, I7 met), the analyses are ROI-focused and no unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map is reported. The reported cluster coordinates derive from exploratory analyses within predefined ROIs rather than an unmasked whole-brain contrast. Therefore the study reports only ROI-based results and does not meet the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5), and thus falls under exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract-level content provided). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual food images). Inclusion criteria not verifiable / not met based on provided text: I4 (no clear within-participant cue>control contrast described), I5 (no confirmation of group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map), I6 (unclear whether whole-brain results are reported as coordinates/figures/supplement), I7 (insufficient reporting of scanner field strength, processing software, and full participant details). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confirmed from the abstract alone. Because the core full text (methods/results) is missing, I cannot verify required criteria—therefore exclude pending full-text availability.

The study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli of the target types (nicotine, alcohol images, drugs, food, sexual). Instead it uses a monetary incentive delay task (monetary cues) in PG and AD patients and contrasts gain/loss cues vs neutral cues. Although whole-brain task analyses are reported (BPM/SPM whole-brain results with SVC) and methodological details (processing software, participant sex/age, cue type) are provided, the key inclusion criteria requiring drug/natural reward visual cue-reactivity and a within-subject contrast of drug-cue>control or natural-reward-cue>control are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study should be excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and explicitly states that “A voxelwise approach was not completed for this analysis,” meaning no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map is provided. Exclusion ID met: E3. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual cannabis stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrast of cannabis cues vs neutral/control stimuli), I7 (reported participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude per E3.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based task activation analyses and does not present any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinate tables/figures that would qualify as whole-brain results. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of drug [alcohol] cue-reactivity using visual cues), I4 (within-participant contrast drinking cues > neutral/control reported), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map provided), I6 (no whole-brain coordinates/figures/supplementary whole-brain results reported that could substitute). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis per E3.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients. It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral), performs group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (one-sample t-test; multiple regression controlling covariates) with appropriate multiple-comparison correction and reports cluster results (tables/figures). Relevant details are provided: participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual cigarette-related and pleasant (natural reward) stimuli (I3). The paper reports within-subject GLM contrasts of cigarette-related and pleasant versus neutral pictures (I4), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and coordinates/figures (I5, I6). Participant age and sex are reported and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) and detailed imaging parameters are provided. However, the manuscript as provided does not report the MRI scanner field strength (e.g., 1.5T or 3T), so criterion I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because all inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is missing, the study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the modality and stimulus-type inclusion criterion I3. This is a PET ([15O]H2O) study using audiotaped script-guided mental imagery (auditory/imagery cues), not an fMRI study using visual cues, so it fails I3. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrast: cocaine cues > neutral/control imagery), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps were reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (functional MRI study using visual stimuli) and I7 (the criterion requests reporting of MRI scanner field strength along with other details; while participant age/sex, cue type, and processing software (SPM99) are reported, MRI scanner field strength is not applicable/missing for a PET study). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related and pleasant images to probe cue-related responses and extinction. It reports within-subject contrasts of CSD+ versus CS− and CSP+ versus CS− (drug and natural reward-related cues versus control stimuli). The paper includes group-level whole-brain analyses (see Tables S1–S2, Figures S3–S4) and reports scanner field strength (4T), processing software (SPM8), cue types (cocaine-related and pleasant), and participant demographics (Table 1). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-subject task contrasts and whole-brain maps). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study examines fMRI responses to monetary reward anticipation using arrow cues (a non-drug, monetary task), not visual cue-reactivity to drug-related or natural reward stimuli (e.g., alcohol images, food, sexual cues). Therefore it does not meet I3 (fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) nor I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control). The paper does report group-level whole-brain task results and coordinates (I5, I6) and provides participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength and processing software details (I7). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study reports ROI-based analyses of ten a priori regions and does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Exclusion criteria met: E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues vs neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis) and I7 (processing software not clearly reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-subject contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported (tables/figures). Participant age and sex are reported, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager) are provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol stimuli and a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral) at first level. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation analyses (whole-group one-sample t-test for alcohol>neutral with voxel-wise and cluster-extent thresholds; results referenced in Table S3 and Figure S1), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Relevant methodological and participant details are provided (age, sex, cue type: alcohol, scanner field strength: 3T, preprocessing software: SPM8/SPM12). Although the manuscript also includes PPI (connectivity) analyses, it additionally reports unmasked whole-brain task activation maps, so no exclusion criteria (E3–E5) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7 and should be included.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study using visual heroin-related vs neutral images in participants on methadone maintenance (I3). It includes a within-subject contrast of drug cues > neutral/control stimuli (I4). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (p < .0001, cluster-level corrected) with coordinates and axial t-maps (I5, I6). Relevant participant and methods details are provided (age, sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, SPM5 preprocessing) (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and the paper is empirical with original human fMRI data. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual (audio-visual) smoking and nonsmoking stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (smoking cue > nonsmoking cue) and conducts voxel-wise, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM2 (whole-brain SPMs reported with cluster results and coordinate tables/figures). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM2) are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, refs) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7.
