The study is an fMRI investigation of monetary (natural) reward cues presented visually and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps using AFNI on a 3T scanner (meets I3, I5, I6, I7). However, it does not report a within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control (neutral) stimuli: contrasts center on effort levels (low, high, unknown) and feedback, not reward cue vs neutral control. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not satisfied, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues that reports within-participant contrasts ("smoke > control") and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANOVA and ANCOVAs) with results presented in tables/figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using audiovisual (visual) stimuli in abstinent heroin-dependent participants. The study reports within-subject contrasts (heroin vs neutral) and a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects ANOVA with cluster-corrected maps and peak coordinates. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and is original human fMRI data). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol-related cue reactivity using visual stimuli (neutral geometric shapes paired with alcohol) with within-subject contrasts comparing CS+ > CS−. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides peak coordinates in tables/figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete: provided content contains only the reference list, title, authors, journal, and DOI but lacks introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The title indicates an fMRI study of cue-induced smoking craving in virtual environments (suggesting visual nicotine cues), so I3 (fMRI study assessing drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) appears to be satisfied based on available metadata. However, critical inclusion criteria cannot be verified: I4 (within-participant drug cues>control contrast) is not reported, I5/I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables/figures) are not present, and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type details, scanner field strength, processing software) are not available. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confirmed from the truncated content. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study must be excluded pending access to the full article.

This is an fMRI study that tested cue-reactivity using visual drug-related words versus matched neutral words in individuals with cocaine use disorder and controls. It includes within-participant drug>neutral contrasts, reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM2 analyses with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates (Table 2 and figures), and provides participant demographics (age/sex reported in Table 1), cue type (cocaine), MRI field strength (4T), and processing software (SPM2). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is referenced but not required. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related BOLD fMRI study using visual drug cues (500-ms cocaine, sexual, aversive, neutral images) with within-subject contrasts (cocaine>neutral). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results and explicitly states cluster-corrected whole-brain results (Table 2 and whole-brain analyses), while also reporting ROI findings. Participant age and sex (mean age 44.4, males), cue types, scanner field strength (Siemens 3T) and processing software (SPM8, AFNI used for cluster correction) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not non-empirical, and within-subject contrasts and unmasked whole-brain task effects are presented). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with a within-subject food>control contrast (food–control) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (coordinates, cluster statistics, FWE corrections and exploratory whole-brain maps). Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is a resting-state fMRI connectivity/graph-theory analysis in nicotine-dependent smokers and controls; it does not involve a task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual stimuli. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only resting-state analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type = nicotine, MRI field strength 3T, and processing software such as FSL and AFNI). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a task-based cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise statistical map), I6 (not applicable — no whole-brain task results reported in text/tables/figures). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues in a within-subjects, placebo-controlled design. It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking vs control/fixation) and a group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise repeated-measures ANOVA (with FDR-corrected vSTR findings and whole-brain exploratory results reported in tables/figures). Participant age and sex are reported (n=12, ages 21–26, 10 men/2 women), cue type (nicotine/smoking), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM2) are all specified. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (personal and standard smoking vs nonsmoking images). It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking>nonsmoking cues (personal and standard), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected, reported in text/figures and Supplementary Table 2). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, includes task whole-brain maps). Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and the study should be included.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual alcohol picture stimuli, reporting within-participant contrasts of alcohol vs. neutral cues and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (3dLME) with cluster correction. Participant age and sex, cue type, field strength, and processing software (AFNI) are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (tobacco) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The within-subject contrasts include smoking-related cues > neutral control (smoking minus neutral) for both Crave and Resist conditions. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using mixed-effects (FLAME) and results are reported with cluster-thresholded statistical maps, tables, and figures. Relevant metadata are reported: participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (FSL). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual, natural reward-related and emotional stimuli (IAPS) in cocaine-dependent and control participants, testing neural reactivity to positive and negative images. It reports within-subject contrasts (positive>neutral and negative>neutral) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM8 with cluster correction, and provides coordinates/tables/figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (positive/negative natural rewards), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) and should be included.

This is an fMRI study using visual video cues (heroin vs neutral) and assesses cue-reactivity. It includes within-subject contrasts (heroin cue vs neutral cue estimated per subject via AUC% beta-model) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise factorial analyses with thresholded maps and coordinates (Table I, figures). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (1.5T GE Signa LX), and processing software (AFNI) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a human fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual images. The paper reports a within-participant contrast (smoking > neutral images) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and coordinates (Table/Figures). Participant age and sex (women, mean age reported), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

The study meets multiple inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (fMRI with visual alcohol cues; within-participant alcohol>neutral contrasts; whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps reported; results presented in tables/figures). However, the full text does not report the MRI scanner field strength (e.g., 1.5T or 3T), which is required by inclusion criterion I7 (information on participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). Because I7 is not met, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of methamphetamine cue-reactivity using visual stimulus pictures in a within-subject, placebo-controlled design. The paper reports a within-participant Methamphetamine Cue>Control Cue contrast and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (Z-statistic maps, cluster-corrected) with tables/figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (methamphetamine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplementary materials are referenced but not required). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical), so the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (Alcohol Pictures Task) with within-participant contrasts of alcohol vs. non-alcohol beverage images. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA) are reported with voxel-wise thresholds and whole-brain cluster correction; results are presented in tables and figures (cluster coordinates and statistics). Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (SPM5, AFNI) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This fMRI study meets several inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6): it is an fMRI investigation of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (videos), reports within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts, and presents whole-brain voxelwise results with tables/figures and FSL 4.1 processing. However, inclusion criterion I7 is not satisfied in the provided full text: although participant age (23 ± 3 y), cue type (nicotine/smoking), and processing software (FSL 4.1) are reported, essential details on participant sex and MRI scanner field strength are not included in the supplied full text. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete for methods/results/discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (cannabis, sexual, aversive) and reports within-subject contrasts (cannabis > neutral; sexual > neutral). Group-level whole-brain analyses are stated to be provided (Online Resource 2) and the manuscript describes voxelwise analyses and thresholding; reporting whole-brain results in supplementary material/tables satisfies I5/I6. Participant demographics (sex/age), cue types, scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8, AFNI, FSL atlas) are reported. Although primary ROI-constrained analyses are emphasized, whole-brain results are available per the text, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and neutral control images with within-subject contrasts (alcohol cues > neutral and stress > neutral). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level analyses (p<0.001, cluster-corrected) and presents results in figures and supplementary tables. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner (3T Trio/Prisma), and processing software (BioImageSuite, AFNI used for cluster correction) are all reported. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an original, task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (videos) of cigarette-related (drug) and food (natural reward) cues with within-participant contrasts (Smoking>Food, Smoking>Baseline) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (tables/figures, corrected thresholds). Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, 3T scanner, and processing software (FSL/FMRIB tools). The manuscript contains core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion), so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it used an individualized script-driven guided imagery paradigm (auditory/imagery-based cues), not visual stimuli, so it fails the review’s requirement for visual cue-reactivity. Full text appears complete. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrasts of drug-cue vs neutral), I5 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with family-wise error correction), I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/supplement), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type [cocaine/alcohol], scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [AFNI]). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Exclusion is therefore due to failure to satisfy I3 (visual-stimulus requirement).

The full text is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) in abstinent alcoholics and controls, with group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM99). It includes a within-subject contrast of alcohol-associated > control (neutral and scrambled) stimuli, and reports group whole-brain voxelwise results (with volume-of-interest correction) in tables/figures/coordinates. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is alcohol (visual), scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (SPM99) are specified. The article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

(a) Exclusion met: E3 — the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (timecourses extracted from five a priori ROIs with hierarchical/linear models) and does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study assessing alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrast ALC > BEV reported), I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type = alcohol, scanner field strength = 3T, and processing software = FSL). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map provided). Because I5 is required and E3 applies, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrast (alcohol vs control). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-test) and ROI analyses; whole-brain results are described and reported (Table 2, figures). Key study characteristics required by the meta-analysis are reported: participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM5). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not assess cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward visual stimuli. It is a within-subject fMRI study of resting-state network coupling and a working-memory (N-back) task comparing 24-hr nicotine abstinence vs smoking satiety. Inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study assessing drug/natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli) are not met because no drug or natural reward cue paradigm or cue>control contrasts are reported. The paper does report group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses for the working memory task with coordinate reporting (satisfies I5 and I6) and provides participant age/sex, scanner field strength, and processing software, but it does not include cue type (no cue stimuli used), so I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore excluded for not addressing the review objective (no visual cue-reactivity data).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol > soft-drink cues (pretraining and pre-post training contrasts) at the group level. The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and second-level (group) t tests, and the authors state that exploratory whole-brain analyses and whole-brain activations are presented in the online supplement (coordinates/tables are reported). Relevant participant details (male participants, age/clinical characteristics), cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. Core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided text. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: cue-reactivity was elicited using personalized auditory imagery scripts (neutral, stress, alcohol) rather than visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts reported: alcohol>neutral, stress>neutral, neutral>baseline), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with FWE correction reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and reported), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and processing software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet I3: the meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, whereas this fMRI study used individualized auditory-guided imagery (audio scripts) to evoke alcohol-cue, stress, and neutral conditions. The full text otherwise contains within-subject alcohol-cue > neutral contrasts (I4), reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (I5) with coordinates/figures (I6), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner strength and processing software details (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cues (audiovisual videos) with a within-participant smoking>nonsmoking contrast. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (contrast maps entered into group analysis) and results are reported with peak coordinates, tables, and figures. Relevant details are reported: participant demographic information (sex, age controlled), cue type (nicotine/smoking), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Full article text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper is an fMRI study of cue-elicited (nicotine) responses using visual stimuli (smoking images). It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking versus neutral (and smoking versus baseline) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (BrainVoyager QX) with corrected thresholds and tables/figures of coordinates. Relevant details are reported: participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Allegra), and processing software. No exclusion criteria are met (results include whole-brain maps rather than only ROI/connectivity or only between-group contrasts without a task map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of visual drug-cue reactivity.

This paper reports a task-based BOLD fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual photographic stimuli, with a within-subject (satiated vs 24-hr abstinent) smoking-cues > control-cues contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (paired and one-sample t-tests) with coordinate tables and figures. Methods include participant age/sex composition, cue type (nicotine/smoking), scanner field strength (4.0 T) and preprocessing/software (SPM5). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria applied: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an fMRI study of reward learning using a visual cue predicting a juice (natural) reinforcer and reports whole-brain analyses, but it does not present a within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control (neutral) stimuli typical of cue-reactivity paradigms. The task probes temporal-difference errors (reward delivery/omission) rather than classic visual cue-reactivity (reward cue vs neutral/control images). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast). It does meet whole-brain reporting and reporting standards (I5, I6, I7), but does not satisfy the critical cue-reactivity contrast requirement. Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs neutral images). It reports a within-participant contrast (smoke > neutral) at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME 1, thresholded Z>2.3, cluster p=0.05) with results presented in tables/figures and described in text. Methods report scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio) and processing software (FSL), and participant demographics are referenced (Table 1). Although a PPI seed-based connectivity analysis is included, the paper also provides unmasked whole-brain task activation maps, so exclusion criterion E4 does not apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; sufficient details are present for meta-analysis inclusion.

Although this is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (meets I3) and includes a within-participant contrast of alcohol cues > control beverage cues (meets I4), and reports participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (1.5T) and processing software (MEDx/SPM99) (meets I7), it does NOT provide whole-brain coverage: authors state they imaged only the anterior third of the brain and lack data for posterior regions (e.g., visual cortex). Therefore I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map with full-brain coverage) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study used gustatory (alcohol taste vs. water) cues delivered in the scanner, not visual cue stimuli (photos/pictures) as required by the meta-analysis. Although visual words (“Alcohol Taste”/“Control Taste”) were displayed, the primary cue modality was taste, so it does not meet I3. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: within-subject alcohol>water contrast (I4), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses reported (I5), acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I6), and relevant participant and MRI details (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Primary cue modality is gustatory (alcohol taste vs. water) rather than visual cue stimuli required by the meta-analysis. Although the task displayed words (“Alcohol Taste”/“Control Taste”), the experimental manipulation and evoked cue were taste-based. The study does meet several inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7): it reports within-participant Alcohol>Water contrasts, provides whole-brain group-level task activation maps and tables/figures, and includes participant demographics, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because it fails I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), it must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (cocaine cues > neutral cues), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME 1 mixed-effects) with thresholding and reported activated clusters/coordinates (table/figures). Participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type (cocaine), MRI field strength (3 T), and processing software (FSL) are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This study is a within-subject fMRI investigation of smokers viewing visual cigarette-related and emotional pictures. It reports a within-participant cigarette>neutral whole-brain, group-level random-effects contrast (voxelwise t-map with cluster thresholding) with peak coordinates in Table 2 and figures. Participant age and sex are reported (N=35, 14 female), scanner field strength (3.0 T) and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-evoked fMRI study of visual drug cues (subliminal cocaine images) in cocaine-dependent humans using a backward-masking paradigm. It reports within-participant contrasts (cocaine vs neutral) and planned group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level t tests (cluster-corrected, voxelwise p<0.005; cluster p<0.05), with peak coordinates and cluster tables/figures described. Participant age range and sex (cocaine-dependent men, 18–55), cue types (cocaine, sexual, aversive), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; thus fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study that includes visual smoking cues (videos) and within-participant contrasts (smoking vs fixation baseline; alcohol vs baseline). Group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain analyses are reported (voxel-wise t tests, cluster-wise inference using FSL). Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue types (alcohol taste and smoking visual), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Although the alcohol cue was a taste paradigm, the presence of visual smoking cues satisfies the review’s visual-stimuli requirement. Full article methods, results, and discussion are provided, enabling extraction of whole-brain activation maps and coordinates. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using validated cigarette-related visual cue videos (I3). It includes within-participant contrasts of cigarette cues versus neutral cues (crave-allow vs neutral; crave-resist vs neutral) (I4). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise using FSL/FLAME with cluster correction and results reported as cluster maps and coordinate tables (I5, I6). The manuscript reports participant demographic/treatment information (Table 1), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT), satisfying reporting requirements (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-participant task activation maps (E3–E5 not applicable). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria, and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study is NOT a visual cue-reactivity fMRI study. It uses a probabilistic delay discounting (PDD) task with monetary rewards (immediate $20 vs delayed/probabilistic monetary options) rather than drug- or natural reward-related visual cues; therefore it does not assess drug/natural reward cue-reactivity. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise task-evoked statistical maps with cluster-correction) and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures described in text). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (not an fMRI cue-reactivity study using drug or natural reward visual stimuli) and I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli or natural reward-cues > control stimuli). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Overall, excluded because it does not address the review objective of visual cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). It contains within-subject contrasts comparing craved food vs. control stimuli (Look Craved > Look Not Craved and Look Craved > Look Neutral) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and tables/figures of coordinates. The manuscript provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8; AFNI used for AlphaSim), meeting all required reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) with within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > neutral cues). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (second-level SPM5 analyses) with results presented in tables and figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations, and references) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (and food/items as appetitive/neutral controls) in alcohol-dependent and control women (ages 18–28). The paper includes within-participant contrasts comparing alcohol vs. control stimuli (e.g., (2×ALC) – (FOOD+ITEM)) and high-risk vs low-risk contrasts, and these were taken to group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using FSL (FLAME1) with cluster correction. The manuscript provides participant age and sex, cue types (alcohol, food, items), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (FSL v4.1.9). The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only connectivity, includes within-subject task maps, empirical data). Accordingly, the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to visual monetary incentive cues (reward vs non-reward contrasts) using a well-described MID task. It includes within-participant contrasts of reward>non-reward, reports group-level whole-brain statistical maps (voxelwise results, corrected and shown in figures/tables), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (monetary visual cues), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (AFNI). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Monetary cues are interpreted here as natural reward-related cue-reactivity relevant to the review objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures) with within-subject contrasts (alcohol > beverage and alcohol > control). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM96/MEDx3.3; Talairach normalization, cluster thresholds reported) and results are reported as regional activations (Table 2, figures) and correlation maps. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type (alcohol visual), scanner field strength (Philips 1.5 T), and processing software (SPM96/MEDx3.3) are all provided. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

The meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity studies using visual stimuli (I3). This study used a gustatory taste paradigm (alcohol taste vs. juice delivered via gustometer), so it does not meet I3 and therefore is ineligible. It does meet other inclusion criteria: within-participant Alcohol>Control contrast (I4), reports whole-brain group-level analyses/coordinates and figures (I5, I6), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking (cigarette) videos with a within-subject Cigarette Cues > Neutral Cues contrast, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) in tables and figures. Participant age range and sex information, cue type (nicotine/cigarette), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL 4.1) are reported. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues in methadone maintenance patients. It reports within-subject contrasts of heroin-related stimuli > neutral stimuli (predose and postdose), and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FSL mixed-effects, reported activation maps and tables/figures, uncorrected threshold and cluster extent). Key methodological details are provided: participant ages and sex distribution, cue type (heroin visual images), scanner field strength (3-T), and processing software (FMRIB Software Library/FSL). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study using visual monetary cues (reward, neutral, punishment) in a within-subject randomized crossover design; contrasts include reward>neutral for anticipation and outcome. Group-level, voxelwise analyses were performed (FLAME 1+2) and whole-brain PPI results are reported with cluster-extent correction and peak coordinates (ACC, OFC, insula). Participant age/sex, cue type (monetary reward), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Although the primary NAcc analysis used small-volume correction, qualifying whole-brain task-evoked connectivity maps and peaks are provided and described. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met.

This is an fMRI study of cue reactivity in cocaine use disorder using visual stimuli (videos of cocaine and food). The authors report within-subject contrasts of cocaine > food cues and provide voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level activation results (cluster sizes, brain regions, and cluster-correction details) using AFNI on a Siemens 3T scanner. Participant age and sex are reported. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s stimulus and task-activation requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (the paper reports only functional connectivity analyses—ICD and seed-to-voxel—without reporting a whole-brain task-evoked activation map) and E5 (results are reported as between-group connectivity contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (the paper reports participant age/sex, cue type [food], MRI field strength [3T], and processing software [SPM5, BioImage Suite]). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the cue exposure used personalized guided auditory imagery, not visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant contrast of visual drug/natural-reward cues > control stimuli is presented in this paper), and I5 (no whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise activation maps are provided). Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and should be excluded.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract provided). The study is an fMRI investigation of cannabis cue-reactivity using backward-masked visual cannabis cues and reports within-subject cannabis>neutral contrasts and voxelwise results (p<.01, k>121) in multiple brain regions, suggesting whole-brain analyses. However the abstract does not report essential methodological details required by I7 (participant age, MRI scanner field strength, and processing software). Because all inclusion criteria must be verifiable and I7 is not met in the provided content, I must exclude the study pending full-text review. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I7. Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text incomplete: true.

This is an empirical neurophysiology/TMS study, not an fMRI study. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast of smoking cues > control stimuli was reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a functional MRI study), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked fMRI map), I6 (no whole-brain fMRI results reported in any format), I7 (does not report MRI scanner field strength or processing software). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails the required fMRI-related inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcoholic drink images) assessing cue-reactivity during a PIT task (I3). The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol versus water background stimuli (alcohol>water PIT parametric modulator) (I4). Group-level, voxel-wise whole-brain analyses are reported (exploratory whole-brain voxel-wise analysis with coordinates and significance, including FWE-corrected SVC at x=18,y=6,z=-12) satisfying whole-brain evidence and coordinate reporting (I5, I6). Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; contains whole-brain task activation maps; empirical task-based fMRI). Full text appears complete. Therefore, include.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E4. The study reports ICA-based task analyses and component-level GLM contrasts but does not present an unmasked, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked activation map for drug>control or reward>control. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task fMRI with visual drug and natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant contrasts: drug-related > neutral computed via component beta-weights), I7 (participant age/sex reported, cue types specified, scanner field strength 1.5T, and processing software SPM8 reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported), I6 (not applicable because qualifying whole-brain results are absent; figures show ICA component maps, not voxelwise task activation maps). Because the meta-analysis requires whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and this study provides only ICA/network-level task modulation without an accompanying unmasked voxelwise activation map, it must be excluded under E4.

This is an fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (participants held and viewed a cigarette vs neutral objects). It reports within-subject contrasts of cigarette>neutral cues (cue main effects and instruction×cue interactions), conducted with voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise ANOVA, Talairach normalization) and reports activation coordinate tables/figures. Participant age and sex (male-only), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5 T GE Signa), and processing software (NIS, AFNI) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The paper reports an empirical fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs non-smoking video clips), with within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > non-smoking cues). Analyses were voxel-wise, group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM2 results reported with coordinates and figures/tables. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM2) are provided. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures vs neutral IAPS), with within-subject contrasts (CUEalc > IAPSneutral). Group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses were performed using SPM/BPM and report whole-brain familywise-error–corrected results and coordinate tables/figures. Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM8, VBM8, BPM) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain task activation maps are reported; results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (cocaine words) and includes a within-subject cocaine>neutral contrast and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM8). However, all reported task analyses are ROI-based (small-volume corrections within a priori ROIs) and the paper does not present or describe an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the drug cues>control contrast. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting).

The full text reports an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual picture stimuli in alcohol-dependent participants, with a within-participant contrast of alcohol cues > non-alcohol beverage cues. Group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses were performed using SPM5 (thresholded maps reported at p<.005, cluster extent 15 voxels) and results are presented in tables/figures (coordinates and images). Relevant methodological details are provided: cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (Philips 3.0T), processing software (SPM5), and demographics are referenced (Table 1) indicating age/sex information is reported in the full text. The article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study of cue reactivity using visual stimuli (opioid, sexual, aversive, neutral) in patients with OUD. It reports within-participant contrasts (drug vs neutral and session × stimulus effects) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain ANOVA with reported cluster k, Z and MNI coordinates). Whole-brain results are described in text and figures/tables (cluster in ventral striatum/mOFC). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, scanner field strength (Siemens Tim Trio 3T) and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so core article content appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study evaluates visual smoking cues and includes within-subject contrasts (smoking > control) and group-level voxelwise analyses reported with coordinates, and reports scanner field strength and processing software; however, all reported task-activation analyses were restricted to a pre-specified anatomical mask created with WFU PickAtlas (i.e., analyses were not unmasked whole-brain voxelwise results). Thus it does not provide unmasked whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps required for inclusion. Exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/masked analyses without whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (fMRI with visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant smoking>control contrast), I6 (coordinates/figures reported), and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, processing software described). Inclusion criterion I5 (unmasked whole-brain group-level analysis) is NOT met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, within-subject fMRI study using visual cue videos (cocaine and food) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (SPM8) with cluster- and FWE-corrected results. It includes within-participant contrasts (cocaine>neutral, food>neutral and fixation baseline), reports relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (4T), and processing software. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study used task-based ICA (group spatial ICA with temporal sorting) to derive network-level betas (DMN, ECN, SN) and reports component spatial maps and component betas (Smoke, Food, Smoke-Food) rather than presenting a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map or coordinate tables for drug>control or natural reward>control. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (ICA/task-based connectivity without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task fMRI with visual smoking and food cues), I4 (within-participant contrasts: smoke, food, and Smoke–Food), I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength, and software). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map provided), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported as coordinates/voxelwise maps/clearly described task maps). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports human fMRI BOLD responses to visual alcohol-related and neutral beverage cues and affective images, meeting the review objective. It includes within-participant contrasts of cue responses (alcoholic vs neutral/positive/negative images) and reports group-level whole-brain activation results (referenced Fig.4 and table S3), with coordinates provided in supplement. Participant age range and sex are reported in the text (age 21–65, and sex controlled for in analyses); cue type is alcohol. Scanner details and processing software are likely reported in the supplementary methods (referenced as (12) and table S1/S3), which is acceptable per inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-subject contrasts of high-calorie food images versus matched non-food control images, and includes group-level voxelwise (whole-brain) analyses (exploratory whole-brain contrasts and whole-brain correlation analyses reported with coordinates). Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is food, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM99) are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task-evoked whole-brain maps, and is empirical).

The article is an empirical fMRI study using visual cannabis cues and matched neutral control images (cannabis vs control within-participant contrast). Group-level whole-brain task effects are reported (main effects per group whole-brain corrected) and between-group contrasts include whole-brain-corrected results outside ROIs. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (cannabis visual stimuli), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The article is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol beverage pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > control (alcpic > con), conducts group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses using SPM8 with cluster-wise correction, and presents results in tables/figures. Methods report scanner field strength (GE 3T), processing software (SPM8), cue type (alcohol), and participant demographic information (age- and sex-matched groups referenced in Table 1). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol and non-alcohol beverage images) in college-aged participants. The study reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol > non-alcohol images and repetition effects, and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with cluster correction; results are described in text, tables, and figures. Participant age range and sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T Allegra), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues in an alcohol-dependent sample and healthy controls. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > control stimuli (e.g., Alcohol_nogo > Non-alcohol_go), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses with cluster-level FWE correction (tables/figures of coordinates provided). Relevant metadata are reported (participant age/sex proportions, cue type = alcohol, 3T Siemens scanner, SPM8 preprocessing). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity visual fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs) is present.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3); it reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > beverage control cues (I4); group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed and reported (SPM99; significant clusters reported and corrected p-values) fulfilling whole-brain evidence (I5); whole-brain results are presented as figures and Talairach coordinates/tables (I6); and participant demographics (male/female college students), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM99) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) with heroin-related > neutral within-participant contrasts. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses (two-sample t-tests) and provides region results (tables/figures) corrected via Monte Carlo simulation; preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8) and scanner field strength (3T) are reported. Participant age/sex and cue type (heroin) are described (male participants; see Table 1). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain results are reported; not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, reporting within-participant contrasts of alcohol-associated versus control pictures, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with reported clusters/tables and figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM99) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs. matched neutral images). It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking > neutral) for encoding and retrieval phases. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and corrected (cluster-corrected p<0.05) with results reported in a table of coordinates (Table 2) and figures. Relevant details are provided: participant age and sex distribution, cue type (nicotine), MRI scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (FSL). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied.

This fMRI study examined smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reported within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > neutral cues, and it provides participant age/sex, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI). However, group-level analyses were conducted using an a priori ROI approach (six 5-mm spheres) and results are reported for ROIs; no unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps, coordinate tables, or whole-brain figures are reported. Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual smoking and neutral images, with within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral) reported. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using FSL/FEAT (FLAME) with clusterwise thresholding (Z>2.3, p=0.05) and results presented as tables of coordinates and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) apply.

The full text reports an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity task using visual stimuli with an within-participant ALC>BEV contrast, and provides participant age/sex info, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) (satisfies I3, I4, I7). However, all reported imaging analyses are ROI-based (ventral striatum percent signal change from a priori spheres) and the article presents no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps or whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplementary materials. Therefore it reports only ROI analyses and lacks the required whole-brain task-evoked map (meets exclusion E3). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. First-level within-subject contrasts include highly desirable > less desirable food images and all food > non-food images. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level analyses were performed (paired t-tests), with coordinates reported (32,10,10) and cluster-level FWE-corrected p-values, indicating whole-brain results rather than ROI-only. Key methodological details required by the meta-analysis are reported: participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain results reported as tables/figures/coordinates) and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type=cocaine, scanner field strength=1.5T, and processing software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study did not assess cue-reactivity using visual stimuli — it used script-based guided imagery, an auditory/imaginal induction), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control visual stimuli; primary contrasts are stress vs neutral imagery), and I5 (authors state limited brain coverage: only 14 of 19 Talairach slices were obtained, indicating insufficient whole-brain coverage for a true whole-brain task-evoked map). Exclusion criteria: none of E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts and necessary sample/scanner/software details. However, the analyses focus on an a priori right ventral striatum ROI (extraction of percent signal change) and the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, coordinates, or tables. Thus inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met and the study meets exclusion E3 (only ROI analyses reported). Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on E3 despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This is a BOLD fMRI study using visual marijuana cues in treatment-seeking, marijuana-dependent participants. It reports within-subject contrasts (MJ cues > Non-MJ cues) at the group level using random-effects GLM analyses. Although primary statistical correction was conducted within an a priori ROI mask, the authors explicitly provide unmasked whole-brain group-level statistical maps (interactive display) and describe whole-brain processing (normalization, smoothing, random-effects analysis), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Relevant participant demographics, cue type (cannabis), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (SPM2, AFNI 3dClustSim) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual tobacco advertisements as cues (nicotine). It reports within-participant contrasts (tobacco > control advertisements) and group-level second-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5; cluster-level FDR-corrected maps and thresholded statistical parametric maps described; supporting tables referenced). Participant age and sex (male, ages reported), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and neutral controls, reporting within-subject contrasts (heroin-related > neutral) and group-level, whole-brain mixed-effects analyses (FLAME) with cluster-corrected voxelwise results. The paper reports participant ages and sex (all male), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT). Results are reported in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject task effect and whole-brain maps). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is a within-subject fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity using visual (word) stimuli and reports cannabis>neutral contrasts, participant age/sex (males 18–30), cue type (cannabis), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). However, all reported statistical analyses were performed within a priori regions-of-interest with small-volume corrections and ROI-based contrasts; the paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (whole-brain evidence). Consequently the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is a resting-state fMRI ROI-based functional connectivity study of smokers vs. controls and smoker subgroups; it does not assess task-based cue-reactivity using visual drug or natural reward cues, and it contains no within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus contrasts or group-level whole-brain task activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only region-of-interest analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses with no whole-brain task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a task fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cues > control contrast), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I6 (no whole-brain task results reported), I7 (does not report cue type/task-related cue information required). Full text appears complete and empirical, but because it is resting-state ROI connectivity (not task-based cue-reactivity), it does not match the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). It includes within-subject contrasts of food>control (food vs. scrambled control pictures) across runs, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM5 (3T scanner) with tables/figures of activations and thresholding details. Participant age, sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength, and processing software are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation with within-subject marijuana cue > control contrasts and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (satisfies I4, I5, I6, I7). However, it used a tactile cue-exposure paradigm (marijuana pipe and pencil) rather than visual stimuli; therefore it does not meet I3 (requirement for visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues. It includes within-participant contrasts of ‘favourite drinks > neutral cues’ and reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level analyses (P<0.001 uncorrected; whole-brain results and coordinates reported in Table 1 and figures). The paper provides participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study in human smokers using visual smoking cues (ISIS images) and neutral control images, with a within-subjects crossover design. The authors modeled smoking and non-smoking events and report group-level random-effects, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (SPM2) with reported activation clusters (uncorrected p<0.0001, cluster threshold) and tabulated results. Although the smoking>neutral contrast yielded no significant differences, that within-participant contrast was performed and reported (null result), satisfying I4. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM2). The full text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity task but used gustatory (taste) cues (alcohol taste vs litchi control), whereas the meta-analysis requires visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant alcohol>control contrast reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with mixed-effects FLAME), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (cue modality is gustatory, not visual), I7 (scanner field strength not reported in the manuscript). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures and beverage/visual control pictures). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol > beverage and alcohol > visual control) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 (thresholded t-maps and reported activations). MRI field strength (Philips 1.5T) and processing software (SPM2) are explicitly reported, and demographic/drinking data are reported (Table 1). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related stimuli, with within-subject contrasts of smoking vs neutral cues entered into group-level analyses. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (task effects and treatment×time interactions) with coordinates and cluster sizes (acceptable per I6). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

The full text is an fMRI study of smoking-related (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-participant contrasts (smoking vs. neutral) and group-level whole-brain, voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses (three-way ANOVA). Whole-brain results are reported (SPM maps and peak coordinates, p<0.001 uncorrected, cluster extent), and methodological details required are provided (participant age/sex information, nicotine cue type, 3.0-T scanner field strength, SPM5 processing). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7 and is included.

This full-text reports an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) with a within-participant contrast (smoking cues > neutral stimuli), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) reporting coordinates and statistical maps. Participant characteristics (age, sex), cue type, scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software are provided. The manuscript contains complete core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) with within-subject contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) in nicotine-deprived smokers. The manuscript reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength (1.5 T), and use of custom MATLAB processing scripts. However, all reported fMRI analyses were region-of-interest (ROI)-based using predefined ROIs; no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps are reported or described. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Decision: EXCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs neutral pictures) in alcohol-dependent adults. The study reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) at two time points (T0, T1) and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level ANOVA) with thresholded statistical maps and reported clusters. Scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (AFNI) are specified; cue type is alcohol. Demographic information is indicated as presented in Table 1 (participants described as adults and group demographics discussed). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3–I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an fMRI study with whole-brain, cluster-corrected results (satisfying I5) and it reports necessary methodological details (scanner field strength, processing software, participant age/sex and cue type — satisfying I7) and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures (I6), it does NOT present a within-participant, whole-brain contrast of visual alcohol cues > control visual stimuli. The primary reported contrasts are taste-outcome (alcohol taste vs water taste) and prediction-error (PE) effects during taste delivery rather than cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. The authors do not report a whole-brain cue (visual Alcohol word) > control cue contrast or equivalent cue-reactivity map, so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I3 and I4.

Only the abstract/full text excerpt is available (fulltext_incomplete=true). The paper is an fMRI study of nicotine cue exposure in virtual environments, so I3 is met. However the provided text does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4 not verifiable), does not describe group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps or coordinates/figures (I5/I6 not verifiable), and lacks required methodological details (participant sex, scanner field strength, processing software) to meet I7. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are explicitly met based on the abstract, but inability to verify key inclusion criteria due to incomplete full text necessitates exclusion. Full text is incomplete; request full article to reassess.

Full text provided appears to be only the abstract/metadata (no full article text with methods/results/discussion). Based on the abstract, the study is an fMRI task using visual heroin cues and reports whole-brain activations; thus it appears to meet I3, I4, I5, and I6. However, the full text is incomplete so key details cannot be verified (participant ages are not reported in the abstract, and availability of unmasked, group-level whole-brain statistical maps or coordinates cannot be confirmed). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm I7 (reporting of participant age and sex and other required details) and cannot reliably confirm all inclusion criteria or absence of exclusion criteria. Therefore I exclude the study pending full-text availability.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that uses visual stimuli signaling impending delivery of chocolate milk (orange triangle/blue star). It includes within-participant contrasts of anticipatory cues (anticipation: chocolate milk vs tasteless solution) and receipt (chocolate milk receipt vs tasteless solution), and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with small-volume corrections) using SPM8 on a 3.0T scanner. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise t-tests with whole-brain family-wise error correction) using AFNI on a 3T scanner. Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength, and processing software are reported. Although the alcohol cue contrast yielded no significant treatment effects, the required within-subject contrast and whole-brain maps were performed and reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, supplementary material referenced).

Full text is not available (webpage inaccessible); only title/metadata are provided. Cannot verify whether study used fMRI visual cue-reactivity or reported whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps. Therefore cannot confirm required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be confirmed: I3 (uncertain if fMRI visual cue-reactivity), I4 (uncertain if within-participant cue>control contrast reported), I5/I6 (uncertain if group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported or coordinates provided), I7 (uncertain if participant demographics, cue type, scanner strength, processing software reported). No exclusion criteria could be confidently applied from the available information. Because full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine-dependent smokers using visual smoking cues with within-subject contrasts (smoke vs. rest and smoke vs. neutral). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (thresholded maps reported and shown in figures/supplement) and describes methods (SPM8), scanner field strength (3T), and participant age/sex. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (drug cue, within-participant contrast, whole-brain group maps, acceptable reporting formats, and required participant/scan/method details).
