No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a resting-state functional connectivity study relating alexithymia, craving, and insula/vmPFC rsFC in smokers; it does not present any task-based drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, nor within-participant contrasts of drug-cues > control stimuli, nor task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without a task activation map). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrasts), I5 (no task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise map). No inclusion criteria are satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract provided). The abstract documents an fMRI study using visual movie cues (e.g., a “heroin puffing” movie and sexual content), so inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI study assessing drug/natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) is satisfied. However the abstract does not provide evidence for a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (I4), does not confirm a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (I5) nor that whole-brain results were reported in acceptable forms (I6), and does not report participant age/sex, scanner field strength, or processing software (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract. Given the incomplete full text and inability to verify required inclusion criteria, the study must be excluded pending full-text availability.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (images of alcohol and soft drinks) and an implicit approach-avoidance task. It reports within-subject contrasts that compare alcohol versus neutral (soft-drink) conditions (e.g., approach alcohol>avoid alcohol and the interaction (approach alcohol>avoid alcohol)>(approach soft drink>avoid soft drink)). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (stated as available in Supplementary Table S1), and main results and ROI and SVC results are described. Participant age/sex (male-only), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains task activation maps, empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food stimuli (natural reward) and reports within-subject contrasts of food>control pictures. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (thresholds, cluster criteria, Table 1, figures), with coordinates and small-volume corrections for a priori ROIs. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3 T) and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core article content appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete (only acknowledgments and references provided). Inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI study assessing natural reward-related visual cues — food) appears satisfied based on title. However I4 (within-participant contrast of food cues > control), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), I6 (clear reporting of whole-brain results), and I7 (reported participant age/sex, cue type details, scanner field strength, processing software) cannot be confirmed from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met, but because core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are missing, we cannot verify required analyses or whole-brain results. Therefore the record is excluded due to incomplete/full-text unavailability for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (drug words) with within-subject contrasts (drug vs. neutral words). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects ANOVA) with cluster-corrected results and lists coordinates (Table 1, figures). Methods report participant demographics (age, gender), cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (4T), and processing software (SPM2). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity that used visual stimuli (as well as auditory) and within-subject contrasts comparing food cues to neutral nonfood stimuli and high-ED vs low-ED foods. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise using SPM5 with reported statistical maps, cluster thresholds, coordinates, and figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and limitations and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cue videos to assess cue-reactivity in patients with alcohol dependence and MDD. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol scenes vs mosaic control, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLM and random-effects) with FDR correction and clusters/coordinates reported in tables and figures. Methods report participant demographics, cue type (alcohol drinking scenes), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so full text appears complete. All required inclusion criteria (I3–I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a real-time fMRI neurofeedback investigation using smoking videos (visual nicotine cues) and includes within-participant analyses relating smoking cue responses to baseline (so I3 and I4 are satisfied). Participant/sample and scanner/processing details are reported (male participants, ages/demographics table, 3T scanner, SPM8), satisfying I7. However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked activation map for drug-cues > control stimuli (no voxelwise task activation contrasts for smoking>nonsmoking are presented). The reported whole-brain voxelwise results are seed-based functional connectivity (FC) maps and ROI analyses rather than a task-evoked activation map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports seed-based connectivity without a corresponding whole-brain task activation map). Conclusion: EXCLUDE (does not provide the required whole-brain task-evoked activation results).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual drug stimuli (drug words) and cocaine cues, with within-subject contrasts (drug word > fixation and drug word > neutral word). The authors report group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (they state testing whole-brain diagnosis × DAT1 interactions at p < 0.05 FWE voxel-level) and also report ROI and composite results; methods list scanner field strength (4T) and processing software (SPM8), and participant sex counts (Table 1 referenced). Core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore the manuscript satisfies I3–I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only nor connectivity-only).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity that reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral/control stimuli and whole-brain task-evoked results (coordinates, cluster statistics, and figures). The paper describes a group-level, voxelwise analysis with whole-brain activations and provides tables/figures of coordinates (acceptable per I6). Cue type (alcohol) and participant sample are described; fMRI acquisition/analysis details are referenced and likely provided in supplementary material (acceptable). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject contrast of smoking cues vs neutral cues, and it reports participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM2). However, all reported group-level voxelwise results were presented within an a priori fronto-limbic mask (mask-restricted voxelwise results) and the paper does not present or describe an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map. Because results are reported only within a regional mask (i.e., effectively ROI/mask-limited voxelwise analysis) and no whole-brain task map is provided, this meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI/mask-only reporting) and therefore fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine cue reactivity using dynamic visual stimuli (movie smoking scenes). It includes a within-subject contrast of smoking versus matched nonsmoking control scenes, reports group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures, and provides participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked task effect).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (meets I3) with a within-subject contrast of alcohol cues > non-alcohol beverage stimuli (ALC–BEV) (meets I4). Relevant methodological details (participant age range, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software FSL v4.1.9) are reported (meets I7). However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) based (predefined VS, mPFC, OFC spheres) and the paper does not present any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain results in text/tables/figures. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion is warranted because no unmasked whole-brain task activation map is provided.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual reward cues (images signaling cigarette puffs and monetary reward) during a task. The authors report within-subject contrasts (money > neutral and puff > neutral) for reward anticipation and submitted first-level contrasts to a second-level random-effects ANOVA, yielding voxelwise clusters (reported cluster sizes and figures), consistent with group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps. Relevant details are reported: participant age and sex, cue types (nicotine/puff and monetary), MRI field strength (3.0T Siemens Allegra), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual pictorial stimuli. It reports within-subject smoking-cue > control-cue contrasts, and group-level, whole-brain (random-effects voxelwise) analyses with results presented in tables/figures (coordinates and images). Scanner field strength (1.5T), processing software (SPM2), and participant sex/age information are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports a within-subject contrast of smoking-related > neutral cues, analyzed with a whole-brain random-effects GLM at the group level and presents whole-brain results in the text/figures (though some effects were uncorrected). Relevant methodological details are reported (sex of participants, cue type: nicotine/smoking images, MRI field strength 3T, and processing software Brainvoyager). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without whole-brain task effect, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3–I7 and is suitable for the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol but used olfactory (ethanol odor) stimuli rather than visual stimuli, so it fails inclusion criterion I3 (must use visual stimuli). Met inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrasts: ethanol odor > neutral air), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables and text), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software provided). No exclusion criteria were triggered (no E3–E6 violations). Therefore the study is excluded solely because it does not use visual cues (I3 not met). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a resting-state fMRI seed-based connectivity analysis (habenula–striatum) in opioid users, not a task-based cue-reactivity study using visual drug or natural-reward cues. Therefore it fails all required inclusion criteria: I3 (no visual cue-reactivity paradigm), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrast), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I6 (no whole-brain task results reported in tables/figures), and I7 (no cue type reported; although scanner field strength and processing software are reported, the absence of a cue paradigm means I7 is not satisfied). Exclusion criterion E4 applies: the paper reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without any task activation map. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual heroin-related images (meets I3). Individual-level heroin>neutral contrasts were modeled and used in group analyses (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (heroin vs neutral; heroin group > controls) with coordinates and figures (meets I5 and I6). Relevant participant details (age, sex=males only), cue type (heroin), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported (meets I7). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and Tables/Figures; no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (chocolate) cue-reactivity that uses visual stimuli (pictures of chocolate). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., picture of dark chocolate vs. grey control; chocpic) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported peak coordinates and corrected statistics. Participant demographic information (age range 20–30, all female), cue type (food/chocolate), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. Whole-brain task-evoked maps and coordinate tables are provided; results are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is complete but the study used olfactory (aroma) cues rather than visual stimuli. Inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI using visual stimuli) is not met. The study does meet other criteria: I4 (within-participant AO>control contrasts), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results reported with peak coordinates/figures), I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables), and I7 (reports participant information, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software SPM5). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded because it does not use visual stimuli required by the review objective.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage images) with a within-subject ALC>BEV contrast. Analyses were conducted at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise GLMs (SPM8) with correction for multiple comparisons (cluster FWE), and results are reported with cluster coordinates and figures. Methods report MRI scanner field strength (3T Philips), preprocessing/analysis software (SPM8/MATLAB), and participant demographic information (age, sex distribution) and cue type (alcohol). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues with a within-subject alcohol>neutral contrast and group-level whole-brain analyses reported (tables/figures referenced). It reports participant age, cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). However, the full text does not report participant sex/gender information, and inclusion criterion I7 requires reporting of participant sex. Because not all required inclusion criteria are met (I7 missing), the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Full text is complete and describes an fMRI study using visual alcohol and natural reward (food) stimuli (I3 met). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (e.g., one-sample win>lose contrast with coordinates and figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I5) and acceptable reporting of coordinates/figures (I6). Participant age/sex, cue types (alcohol, food, gambling), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM2) are reported (I7). However, the manuscript does not present a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (no alcohol>neutral or food>neutral within-subject cue-reactivity contrast is reported). Instead, analyses focus on win>lose (reward) and high>low personal reference and stimulus-category ANOVAs; no unmasked, whole-brain alcohol cue-reactivity contrast is provided. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it lacks the required within-participant drug/natural cue > control contrast (I4 not met).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking>control, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps (t-maps, thresholded with random field theory) and cluster/peak coordinates in tables/figures, and provides participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (fmristat). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using novel visual stimuli (geometric CS paired with IV alcohol) in heavy drinkers. The paper reports within-participant contrasts between CS+ (alcohol-paired) and CS− (saline-paired), including the [CS+ > CS−] contrast (reported as non-significant) and the [CS− > CS+] contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM5 with FWE-corrected cluster statistics and coordinates/figures reported. Participant age and sex (mean age ~24.9; all male), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, within-subject fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues. The manuscript reports (a) cue-reactivity to alcohol images presented visually, (b) within-participant contrasts comparing cue conditions to baseline (e.g., passive viewing of alcohol cues vs baseline) and contrasts of prayer vs other conditions, (c) group-level, whole-brain random-effects robust regressions with cluster-level (Alphasim/FWE) correction and tables/figures of significant clusters, and (d) required methodological details (participant demographics, cue type = alcohol, 3T scanner, preprocessing/analysis with SPM8). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity that meets several inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7): it reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > control (alcohol vs isocaloric control beverage), uses group-level whole-brain mixed-effects analyses with cluster correction and reports results in tables/figures, and provides participant demographics, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). However, it does NOT meet I3 because the primary reward-related cues are gustatory (taste delivery of alcohol vs litchi juice via a gustometer), not visual drug or natural reward stimuli. Although written change-talk statements were visually presented, the cue-reactivity contrast examines taste cues rather than visual cue exposure required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded due to failure to satisfy I3 (visual-stimuli requirement).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). The authors report within-participant contrasts (alcohol > non-alcoholic beverage) and additional contrasts (negative-beverage, positive-beverage), and perform group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (one-sample t-tests and 2×3 ANOVA with voxel-wise thresholds and tables of coordinates). Relevant metadata are reported: participant numbers and matching, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (AFNI). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual picture cues (alcohol, marijuana, polydrug) in at-risk college students and reports within-subject contrasts of drug-related>neutral cues. Whole-brain voxelwise group analyses were performed using FSL/FEAT and significant activations are reported in tables and figures (insula, ACC, caudate, prefrontal, etc.). Participant age and sex are given (10 participants, ages 19–21, 5 female/5 male), cue types specified, MRI scanner field strength reported (Siemens Allegra 3T), and processing software (FSL). Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (core content present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject task regressors for high-calorie, low-calorie, and non-food images and condition × task analyses. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (FWE whole-brain corrected maps; Figures 3–5 and Table 1), and contrasts examine food-related cues relative to control stimuli across glycemic conditions. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3 T), and processing software (BioImage Suite/AFNI/SPM pipeline). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards (food).

The study is excluded because it does not provide the required within-participant drug-cue > control-stimuli contrast (it reports repetition-priming contrasts: non-studied vs studied alcohol/polydrug/marijuana cues rather than drug cues > neutral/control) — inclusion criterion I4 not met. Additionally, the full text does not report participant ages or MRI scanner field strength (acquisition parameters are deferred to an accompanying paper), so inclusion criterion I7 is not met. The study does meet I3 (fMRI study with visual drug/alcohol cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster thresholding reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none of E3–E6 apply). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a resting-state fMRI pharmacologic (KB220Z vs placebo) pilot study in abstinent heroin users, not a cue-reactivity task using visual stimuli. It does not include any within-participant task contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli (I3 and I4 not met). Although group-level whole-brain MVPA maps are reported, they are resting-state/treatment effects rather than task-evoked cue responses, so the required group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is absent (I5/I6 not met). Reporting includes participant age/sex, scanner strength (3T) and processing software (SPM5) but no visual cue type (I7 not met). This study therefore meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking images (I3 satisfied). It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking vs rest/neutral in ROI measures (PSC) (I4 satisfied) and provides participant/sample info, cue type, scanner field strength, and software (I7 satisfied). However, the paper presents results focused on an a priori/isolated ACC ROI (individual ROIs and ROI-based PSC) and does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or coordinate table of whole-brain task effects. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain group-level results (I5 not met) and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Excluded for lack of whole-brain, group-level task activation results required by the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports only ROI-based fMRI analyses and explicitly states it did not perform (or report) whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of drug cue reactivity using visual smoking cues), I4 (within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > control stimuli were analyzed and reported), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM99) are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported), and therefore I6 (acceptable whole-brain reporting) is not applicable. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because the review requires whole-brain task activation maps and this paper provides only ROI analyses, it must be excluded under E3.

This study examines aversive fear conditioning (visual CS paired with an electrical shock) in cocaine users vs. controls, not drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and corrected results), I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/supplement), I7 (reports participant age and sex, MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8)). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (not an fMRI study of drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/reward cues), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues>control stimuli or natural reward cues>control stimuli). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study reports an fMRI experiment using visual alcohol cues (90 alcoholic and neutral beverage images) and includes within-subject contrasts (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages). Group-level, voxelwise statistical maps were generated for each contrast and group (the manuscript explicitly describes generation of individual and group statistical maps and voxel-wise t-tests), satisfying whole-brain task-evoked mapping. Relevant participant demographics (age range, sex distribution), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion decision because the study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual cues and does not include within-participant contrasts of drug-cue>control or natural-reward-cue>control. Instead, it uses a reinforcement-learning task with probabilistic rewards (smiling/frowning feedback). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps of PE-related activity) and I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a cue-reactivity fMRI study using visual drug/natural reward cues), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control or natural-reward-cue>control contrast), I7 (cue type for visual cue-reactivity not applicable/reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E6). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (food) and reports within-participant contrasts of food > nonfood. The manuscript includes group-level voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise subtraction, whole-brain maps/figures and reported MNI coordinates/local maxima for the food vs nonfood contrast), satisfying the whole-brain task-evoked map requirement. Relevant metadata are reported (participant age/sex, cue type: food, scanner: 3.0 T, processing software: AFNI). The study is not ROI-only, not a connectivity/resting-state paper, and not non-empirical. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related (alcohol) and natural reward (positive IAPS) stimuli with within-subject contrasts (alcohol>neutral; positive>neutral; negative>neutral). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM5 (thresholds reported), with results presented in tables/figures (coordinate reporting). Participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes task activation maps). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports first-level within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (combined voxel-wise P<0.001 and cluster-extent thresholds with reported peak MNI coordinates and tables/figures). Participant information (age range 18–65, sex counts), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5/SPM8) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains whole-brain task activation maps).

This study is a behavioral cue-reactivity study using personalized videotaped alcohol cues; the abstract and available full-text metadata describe urge/craving ratings across in vivo and videotape exposures. There is no mention of functional MRI scanning, BOLD measures, neuroimaging methods, scanner field strength, or voxelwise/whole-brain analyses. Therefore it does not meet the key fMRI-related inclusion criteria required for this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an fMRI study assessing cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant fMRI contrast reported), I5/I6 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked map reported), I7 (no MRI scanner or processing software reported). No explicit exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered because the paper is not an fMRI paper rather than violating specified fMRI-analysis exclusions. Full text appears to be incomplete for purposes of confirming imaging details (only abstract/metadata shown), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

The provided content is only a brief summary/abstract and lacks core article sections (methods, detailed results, tables/figures). Inclusion: I3 is met — this is an fMRI study presenting alcohol-related visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria not verifiable: I4 (no explicit report of a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast), I5 (no confirmation of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map), I6 (no evidence that whole-brain results were reported in text/tables/figures), I7 (participant age/sex, scanner field strength, processing software not reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the summary. Because essential inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, exclude; obtain the complete article to reassess.

This empirical fMRI study investigates nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports a within-subject contrast (smoking > neutral). Group-level whole-brain task activation results are presented and cluster-corrected (Z=2.3, p<0.05) with tables and figures. Methods report participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only analyses, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and is appropriate for the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it is a PET study, not a functional MRI (fMRI) study; therefore inclusion criterion I3 (Functional MRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast: drug video > neutral video is reported), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (fMRI modality). I7 (reporting MRI scanner field strength and MRI-specific details) is not satisfied: the paper reports a PET scanner and SPM processing but no MRI field-strength for functional imaging. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of smoking using visual stimuli (meets I3) and includes within-participant contrasts of smoking versus neutral images (meets I4). Participant demographics, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (AFNI) are reported (meets I7). However, the manuscript reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (a priori 4 mm spheres) used to extract beta values for prediction analyses and does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or coordinates/tables of whole-brain task results. Therefore it violates the review’s requirement for whole-brain evidence and meets Exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results). Because I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked map) is not met and E3 applies, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using audio-visual (visual) stimuli, reporting within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking cues and whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with coordinates and cluster-corrected results. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual monetary reward cues (non-drug natural rewards). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of reward cues versus nonincentive control cues (pre-response $1/$10 vs $0; WIN vs HIT), and higher-order reward notification contrasts. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported (with FDR correction) and coordinate tables/figures are provided. Relevant metadata are reported: participant ages and sexes, cue type (monetary reward), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject task effects, and is empirical). Full text content appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based analyses and does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps (meets exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (event-related fMRI of drug cue-reactivity using visual smoking cues), I4 (within-subject contrast of smoking cues > control cues reported), and I7 (reported participant age/sex, cue type—nicotine/smoking, scanner field strength 1.5T, and processing software SPM99). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map is reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage images paired with IAPS emotional pictures). It includes within-participant contrasts comparing alcohol vs non-alcohol cues, reports voxelwise group-level whole-brain analyses with cluster-wise correction, and provides details on participant sex, cue type, 3-T scanner field strength, and AFNI processing. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the article is complete and meets all inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues in alcohol-dependent patients, with within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol versus soft-drink control stimuli (e.g., [alcohol pull > soft drink pull] and related contrasts). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported (including whole-brain FWE-corrected results and supplementary whole-brain tables/coordinates). Methods report participant sex (male), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8); demographic info is presented in Table 1. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts and group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses reported (tables/figures) using SPM5 on a 1.5T scanner. However, the full text does not report participant demographic details for age (mean/SD) or sex breakdown—only eligibility age range is given—so it fails inclusion criterion I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting I7.

The study is excluded because it does not meet I3: cue modality is individualized script-driven guided imagery (auditory/internal imagery), not visual stimuli required by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-subject alcohol-cue vs neutral contrasts present), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/reported), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type—alcohol, scanner 3T, and processing software AFNI reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it is not an fMRI study and does not report any task-evoked whole-brain fMRI results. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (study does not use functional MRI to assess cue-reactivity with visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant fMRI cue>control contrast reported), I5/I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or coordinate tables), I7 (no MRI scanner field strength or processing software reported). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply. Full-text completeness: only abstract/metadata content was available in the record provided, so fulltext_incomplete=true. Primary measures reported are behavioral self-report craving and mood in response to alcohol vs water cues; no imaging data to satisfy the meta-analysis objectives.

This study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria. Met: I3 (an fMRI study using visual cigarette and food cues), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses), and I6 (reports whole-brain results in figures/tables). Not met: I4 — there is no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control (neutral) stimuli or natural reward cues > control stimuli; the main reported contrasts are instruction-based (LATER vs NOW) rather than cue > neutral contrasts. I7 — relevant acquisition detail (MRI scanner field strength) is not explicitly reported in the text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject contrast (smoking cue > neutral cue) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (FDR-corrected activations, whole-brain multiple regression). The manuscript provides participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study reports an fMRI investigation of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs neutral pictures) with within-subject contrasts. The fMRI group performed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (2×2 ANOVA; FWE-corrected results reported; tables/figures present), and psychophysiological interaction and whole-brain cue activations are described. Participant demographics (sex, group sizes) and cue type (nicotine) are reported; fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, and analysis procedures are referenced and described in Methods and Supporting Information, and processing/software for EEG/fMRI analyses (BESA, Scan) are named. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cue videos (nicotine cues) with within-subject contrast 'smoking videos vs control videos.' Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (mixed-effects FLAME, TFCE correction) and results are reported as whole-brain activations (figures and supplementary tables). Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This article is a narrative review summarizing prior fMRI and MRS studies rather than an original empirical human fMRI study. It therefore meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper/review). It does not itself present primary fMRI data with within-participant contrasts of drug-cue > control or natural reward-cue > control (I3 and I4 not met), nor does it present group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or coordinates from a primary analysis (I5/I6 not met). Although the review discusses cue-reactivity findings and reports cue types and some participant characteristics from cited studies, it does not provide the primary-study scanner field strength or processing software as required for inclusion of a primary dataset (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore it must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes within-subject contrasts (food > neutral), reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (exploratory 1-sample t test with Table 2 and Figure 2, FWE-corrected), and provides required methodological/participant details (age, sex, cue type: food, scanner field strength: 3T, preprocessing software: SPM5). All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual reward-related cues (images of a $100 bill vs a blurry rectangle) and reports within-subject contrasts of reward>nonreward. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (z>3.1, cluster-corrected) with results described in text/tables/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (monetary reward), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (90 pictures of alcoholic and neutral beverages). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages) at the individual level and computes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI 3dMVM) with family-wise error correction. Participant age and sex are reported (female, 21–65 years), cue type is alcohol, scanner field strengths (3T GE, 3T Siemens Skyra, 3T Siemens Verio) and processing software (AFNI) are specified. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This study is a human BOLD fMRI investigation using visual natural reward cues (food images). It includes within-participant contrasts (all food > non-food; high-calorie > low-calorie). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with stringent FWE cluster correction and detailed results. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) are met. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

Study meets several inclusion items (I3, I4, I6, I7) — it is an fMRI study of nicotine cue reactivity using visual stimuli, includes within-participant smoking cue>control cue contrasts, reports voxel peak coordinates/cluster peaks, and reports participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner (3T), and processing software (SPM8). However, all task-activation voxel-wise analyses were conducted within an a priori ROI mask rather than as an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task map. Thus it fails I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analysis with no whole-brain results). Therefore exclude.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual (and tactile) cigarette cues. The authors report within-subject cigarette>control contrasts and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (with cluster correction) and provide tables of peak coordinates and figures. Participant age and sex (male; ages 18–45), cue type (cigarette/nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI, FSL, etc.) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual Pavlovian cues and outcome images. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of food-related cues > no-outcome control cues during task (PIT) and presents group-level voxelwise statistical maps (voxelwise, permutation-based testing via FSL Randomise) with reported coordinates and figures; exploratory whole-brain analyses are also noted (Table S1). Participant age/sex reported (n=30 initially, final N reported), cue type = food, scanner field strength = 3T, and processing software = FSL are provided. Analyses include task-evoked activation contrasts ( cue vs no-outcome ) and voxelwise results (small-volume corrected and coordinates), meeting the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study is not an fMRI cue-reactivity study. It is a behavioral clinical pilot comparing craving (VAS) and methadone dose in heroin-dependent patients with and without ADHD. No MRI/fMRI methods, no imaging acquisition, no within-participant fMRI contrasts (drug cues>control), and no whole-brain task activation maps or coordinates are reported. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis requirements for neuroimaging cue-reactivity studies.

This study reports an fMRI experiment using visual food cues (natural rewards) in adolescents, with within-subject task contrasts (go vs no-go trial types and task activity collapsed across food trials) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (3dMVM) reported with cluster coordinates and figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI, ANTs) are provided. The whole-brain task-evoked results are reported in tables/figures (satisfying voxelwise/map requirements). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with within-subject contrasts of food versus nonfood, satisfying the review focus. The manuscript reports first- and second-level GLM analyses, whole-brain regression analyses (FWE-corrected) and presents coordinate-based results and figures of activation (e.g., fusiform, insula, amygdala), meeting the requirement for group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps. Necessary reporting details are present: participant age/sex (15 healthy young males, mean age 23.3), cue type (food), MRI scanner (Siemens Magnetom Verio 3T), and processing software (SPM8). Results include coordinate tables and voxelwise statistics and parametric/whole-brain analyses, so ROI-only or connectivity-only exclusions do not apply. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3/I4/I5/I6/I7 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Although this is an fMRI study that presented visual cigarette cues during an in-scanner Smoking Pleasantness (SP) task and reports participant demographics and MRI details (meets I3 and I7), the manuscript does not report a within-participant task contrast of drug cues > control stimuli nor a whole-brain, group-level task activation map for cue-reactivity. The imaging results focus on an interoceptive attention task (interoception vs exteroception) and resting-state connectivity; the SP task appears used for behavioral ratings and correlational analyses only. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of methamphetamine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (picture-based Methamphetamine Cues Task). The analysis includes a within-participant Methamphetamine Cue > Control Cue contrast and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (FSL/FEAT; cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<.05). Whole-brain activation is reported in figures and Table 1 (coordinates). Relevant participant age/sex details, cue type (methamphetamine), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material is not required for eligibility.

Exclusion met: E3 (study reports only ROI-focused analyses with no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map). The paper centers its primary analyses on an a priori PCC ROI (beta-weights extracted from PCC) and reports a voxel-wise check restricted to the PCC mask; it does not present an unmasked whole-brain, group-level smoking>neutral activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI of nicotine/smoking cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrast smoking cues > neutral control), I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type nicotine, scanner field strength 3T, and processing software FSL). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map provided), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results presented in tables/figures/supplement that would satisfy I5). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given the requirement that a whole-brain task activation map be available, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) visual cue-reactivity. The study used within-subject contrasts of hedonic food images > non-food control images in fasted and fed states, and reported group-level, whole-brain random-effects statistical maps (voxel-wise threshold p<0.01, cluster-level FDR q<0.05) with tables/figures of coordinates. Methods report participant ages/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is not an fMRI task activation study. The paper uses EEG/LORETA for cue-reactivity and DTI structural imaging after tDCS; no group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked fMRI statistical maps are reported. Exclusion criterion E3 applies (no whole-brain fMRI results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli was performed using ERPs) and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength and processing software are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (functional MRI study) and I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked fMRI map). Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirements and is excluded.

This full text reports an empirical fMRI cue-exposure study using visual drug-related stimuli (drug-related pictures) with an within-subject contrast of drug cues > neutral control stimuli. Group-level whole-brain task activation maps are reported (main effect thresholded at p < .05 FWE corrected, with additional whole-brain exploratory analyses reported), and results are presented in figures/tables. Relevant participant details (male adolescents aged 14–19), cue types (cocaine, methamphetamine, heroin/paraphernalia), MRI field strength (1.5T Siemens Avanto mobile scanner), and processing software (SPM12; ArtRepair; INRIAlign) are provided. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (pictures/videos) that assesses cue-reactivity. The authors report within-subject contrasts of smoking versus matched control (smoking minus control: BEGIN S2-T2, END S4-T4, etc.) and use these contrasts in group-level analyses. Analyses were carried out with SPM5 and report whole-brain group-level activations and deactivations (tables/figures referenced), satisfying voxelwise task-evoked maps. Participant demographics (age/sex counts), cue type (nicotine/smoking), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos). The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing smoking vs. non-smoking videos (smoke>non-smoke) and presents whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level task activation analyses (FSL FLAME1, cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) with reported activation coordinates/figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates none of the exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study (N=24) using visual food cues (natural rewards) and nonfood control images, reporting within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood. The paper includes a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis (drink x cue interaction; cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) with figures/tables (Fig.3, Table S2) and ROI analyses. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7), and no exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain results are reported, not only ROI/connectivity/between-group-only or non-empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion justified for meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards (food).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (smoking vs neutral cues), performs whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (FDR-corrected) and whole-brain regression analyses, and provides tables/figures of coordinates and results. Participant information (male-only sample, age/education matching) is reported, as are cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3–I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria E3–E6.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (actual foods presented). It reports within-subject contrasts of food>non-food, and uses group-level whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses with thresholds and coordinate tables/figures. Methods report MRI field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM2); participant sex (2 male, 4 female) and cue type (food) are explicitly reported and participant ages are referenced in Table 1 (subject characteristics) within the full text. Whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures, satisfying the reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to visual natural rewards.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual presentation of cues (participants viewed a live video feed of their hand holding a cigarette), and includes within-subject contrasts comparing cigarette versus control objects. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLM, second-level ANOVA) with tables of coordinates and figures describing significant cigarette>control effects (main effect of cue, Table 3 and Figure 1). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T Allegra), and processing software (AFNI, FSL, etc.). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing smoking-cue delay trials to control and neutral conditions, including a voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain analysis (repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster correction and tables/figures of coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are all reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article is complete for screening purposes. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the paper reports only ROI- and system-level task analyses without reporting any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or tables/figures of whole-brain coordinates, so it meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of a natural reward—food—using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant food>control contrasts were computed). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps or coordinate table are reported). I7 (participant age is not explicitly reported; sex, cue type, scanner field strength and processing software are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) comparing food>nonfood contrasts. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (food vs nonfood) and whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (flexible factorial, two-sample t tests, voxelwise thresholds) with tables/figures and ROI/PPI supplementary analyses. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in a within-subject design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food>control pictures, and group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (exploratory whole-brain analyses and reported clusters/coordinates, with supplementary tables referenced). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), and MRI field strength (3T) are reported. Methods describe voxelwise first- and second-level GLM analyses and small-volume correction with PickAtlas, and whole-brain results are presented in text, figures, and supplementary tables. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Note: processing software is not explicitly named in the provided excerpt, but the analysis approach and use of PickAtlas imply standard voxelwise fMRI processing; supplementary materials likely contain full processing details.

This article is not an fMRI cue-reactivity study. It reports behavioral/clinical factor analysis in an AUD sample and does not include any task-based fMRI methods, visual cue-reactivity paradigms, within-participant drug-cue>control contrasts, or whole-brain task activation maps. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I3, I4, or I5 (nor I6 or I7). No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E6) are specifically triggered beyond failing to meet inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7. Full text appears complete for the purposes of screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-calorie food images). It includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie food > brick walls). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM5 (second-level flexible factorial across subjects) and results are reported as statistical parametric maps and clusters (whole-brain and ROI-corrected spatial extent p-values). Participant demographic information (age, sex), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (appetizing vs bland images) to assess natural reward cue-reactivity. It includes within-subject contrasts (appetizing > bland) at first level and reports group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses (one-sample t tests) with coordinates and figures. Methods report participant ages and sex distribution, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided; supplemental material is noted but not required. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-calorie food images). It includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food cues vs objects (food>control) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory FLAME analyses with cluster correction and Table 4 coordinates). Relevant details (participant age/sex, cue type: food, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software FSL/AFNI/FreeSurfer) are provided. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete: provided content is a website privacy/preferences page, not the article full text. Cannot verify core methods/results. Therefore inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met (unable to verify): I3 (uncertain if this is a functional MRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli), I4 (no evidence of a within-participant contrast of drug/natural cues > control), I5 (no confirmation of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), I6 (no whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text), I7 (no reporting of participant age/sex, cue type details, scanner field strength, or processing software). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3-E6 can be determined from the incomplete content. Fulltext_incomplete=true.

The study is an empirical task-fMRI investigation of responses to personalized cues including favorite-food (a natural reward). However, it does not meet the review's requirement that cue-reactivity be elicited using visual stimuli (I3). This study used personalized guided-imagery auditory scripts presented via headphones (auditory/imagery stimuli), not visual cue presentations. It does meet other inclusion criteria: within-participant contrasts of favorite-food vs control (I4), group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps with FWE correction (I5; results reported as whole-brain clusters/tables; I6 acceptable), and reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5, AFNI) (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because I3 is not satisfied.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural (sexual) reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (erotic pictures). The task disentangled cue (anticipation) vs reward (outcome) phases and modeled cue and control conditions; within-participant contrasts (cue-related responses) and cue>control modeling were performed. Although primary ROI analyses are emphasized, the authors report whole-brain second-level results (noted as presented in Supplementary Figure S3), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps (I5/I6). Participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), and scanner field strength (3-T) are reported; preprocessing/analysis details are referenced in Supplementary Materials (fulfilling I7). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Minor uncertainty concerns explicit naming of processing software in the main text (reported in supplement), reflected in the confidence score.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues with within-participant food>nonfood contrasts and reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner (3T), and SPM5 processing (meets I3, I4, I7). However, the neuroimaging results are derived from a voxelwise analysis restricted to a predefined mask/regions of interest with FWE correction within those ROIs; the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map. Therefore it does not meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and constitutes an ROI-only analysis, triggering exclusion. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results) and E5 (results emphasize interactions/group differences without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task map).

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in treatment-seeking smokers. It includes a within-participant contrast of smoking cues > neutral control (LookSmoking > LookNeutral), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with cluster correction (AlphaSim), and provides relevant methodological details (participant age eligibility, sex distribution in Table 1, cue type nicotine, scanner field strength Siemens Allegra 3.0T, processing software SPM8). Whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures (e.g., Table 2, cluster coordinates, PPI results). All inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (highly palatable vs. moderately palatable and vs. neutral). The manuscript reports whole-brain analyses (explicitly states whole-brain analyses were conducted and reports activations across brain reward circuitry) and refers to Supporting Information for MRI acquisition and processing details. Participant demographics (female, ages 18–25, mean age reported) and cue type (food) are provided; MRI acquisition/processing details are indicated as reported in the Supporting Information, satisfying reporting requirements. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, nor non-empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of smokers viewing visual cigarette-related stimuli (graphic warning labels), assessing neural and behavioral cue-reactivity. It includes within-participant contrasts of LABEL>CONTROL and HIGH>LOW, reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FEAT/FSL) with cluster correction and tables/figures, and provides participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine/ cigarette warnings), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL). Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results and discussion. Recommended for inclusion.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for a whole-brain fMRI cue-reactivity meta-analysis: it is an fMRI study of drug (methamphetamine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (I3); it includes within-participant contrasts of MA cues > neutral/control stimuli (I4); it reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and voxelwise group-level analyses using nonparametric permutation testing and cluster correction (I5); whole-brain results are presented in figures and supplementary materials (I6); and relevant methodological and participant details are reported (cue type, 3T scanner field strength, processing software FSL/BROCCOLI, and demographic reporting referenced in Table 1) (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task activation maps, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion included).

This study examines smoking cue-reactivity with visual stimuli using pCASL perfusion fMRI (nicotine cues vs non-smoking cues) and reports within-subject contrasts (SCs > non-SCs) and participant details (age, sex), scanner field strength (3T) and SPM8 processing — satisfying I3, I4, and I7. However, analyses are reported as ROI-restricted (ROI mask analyses) with no unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map provided; thus it meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only results) and fails to meet I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual heroin-related vs neutral images (visual cues). It includes a within-subject heroin-related > neutral contrast, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and post-hoc contrasts) with whole-brain correction (Monte Carlo simulation). Results are presented in figures/tables and described in text. Participant characteristics (all male, group demographics in Table 1), cue type (heroin), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8; AFNI for cluster correction) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Although this is an fMRI study of nicotine-related visual stimuli and includes within-subject contrasts (graphic > non-graphic) and reports coordinates and methodological details (age/sex, cue type nicotine, 3T scanner, FSL), the group-level analyses were conducted as a priori ROI-masked analyses (amygdala, striatum, insula, DLPFC). The manuscript does not present or describe an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results).

This study does not assess drug-related or natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity: it used a monetary probabilistic feedback/anticipation task (gains/losses) rather than drug cues or natural reward cues (e.g., food, sexual). Therefore it does not provide a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control or natural reward cues > control. It does report group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task analyses (tables/figures) and provides participant age/sex, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI, FSL). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), I7 (demographics, cue type, scanner, software reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (fMRI of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward cues>control). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food and sexual images) in an event-related design with within-subject contrasts (food > baseline; sexual scenes > baseline) that predict behavioral outcomes. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects mean t-images; whole-brain regression analyses thresholded at p<0.001 with coordinates and clusters reported). Participant age and sex (female, 18–19), cue types (food, sexual), scanner field strength (3T Philips), and processing software (SPM2) are provided. Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This article appears to be a narrative review/commentary rather than an original human fMRI empirical study. Full text provided is limited to title, abstract, keywords, and metadata with no methods, participants, results, or figures/tables. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper/review without original human fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none (no I3, I4, I5, I6, or I7 satisfied). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an empirical fMRI study assessing cue-reactivity with visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant contrasts of drug-cues>control), I5/I6 (no group-level whole-brain statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures described), I7 (no participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, or processing software reported). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata), so fulltext_incomplete=true.
