This is an fMRI study of visual food cues in craniopharyngioma patients that includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie ‘fattening’ > low-calorie ‘non-fattening’). Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. However, the manuscript presents results as ROI-based mean z-scores and representative subject images and does not present group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps, coordinate tables, or unmasked whole-brain task activation maps. Because no whole-brain group-level activation maps are reported and the analysis is limited to ROI results, it violates the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (erotic and monetary) assessing cue-reactivity with within-subject contrasts (monetary cue > control; erotic cue > control) at the group level. Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds; coordinates provided), and results are described in text and figures. Participant demographics (mean age, all male), cue types (erotic/sexual and monetary), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM2) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (within-participant alcohol>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I3 (study does NOT use visual stimuli; the cue modality is gustatory — taste of alcohol vs. juice). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because the meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity studies using visual stimuli (I3), this study must be excluded despite meeting other fMRI and reporting criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual sexual cues (natural reward) using a block design. It includes within-participant contrasts (sexual > neutral; sexual > other rewards), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps with coordinates, figures, and statistical thresholds (with FDR correction), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies all listed inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) with right-handed smokers and non-smoker participants (sex and age reported). The authors report within-subject contrasts of smoking versus matched control pictures (BEGIN- and END- stimuli minus control stimuli) and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME, FSL) with FWE-corrected thresholds; results are presented in tables/figures with coordinates. Scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are specified. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts comparing sexual > neutral/emotional control conditions, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM12, random-effects) reporting coordinates, statistical maps, and figures. Relevant participant information (sex, age range), cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplements) is provided. Although sample size is small and exploratory, these factors do not violate inclusion/exclusion criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > fixation), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). However, the paper reports results from predefined ROI analyses (Table 2) and does not present or describe an unmasked, group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinate table/figure covering whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and does not provide whole-brain results in acceptable formats (I6). Exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (appetizing food images) and includes within-participant contrasts of stimulus > baseline (Far + Close > fixation) as well as task contrasts (Far > Close). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level voxelwise tests reported with cluster coordinates and supplemental tables, using SPM8 on 3T data. Participant age and sex distribution, cue type (food), scanner field strength, and processing software are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI with visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-subject cue > control/baseline contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables), and I7 (reported demographics, cue type, scanner, software). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual erotic (sexual) cues in Parkinson’s patients (meets I3) and reports group-level whole-brain task analyses with tables/coordinates (meets I5 and I6). However, the task does not include a within-participant contrast of erotic cues > neutral/control stimuli (analyses focus on parametric subjective-value modulation, decision vs outcome phases, and group interactions), so I4 is not satisfied. Also, although participant age/sex, cue type, and processing software (SPM8) are reported, the manuscript as provided does not report MRI scanner field strength (so I7 is not fully satisfied). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because inclusion criteria I4 and I7 are not met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and reports within-subject contrasts comparing food-related stimuli to non-food control stimuli (Food > Activities). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM8; whole-brain thresholds and clusters provided; tables/figures described). Relevant participant information (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Tim Trio), and processing software (SPM8, CONN for gPPI) are reported. The task elicits cue-related responses and correlates activation with self-reported craving, satisfying the meta-analysis objective of visual cue-reactivity for natural rewards. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task map, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (Coke product and logo advertisements). It reports within-participant contrasts of natural reward-related cues vs. control (Coke product ads > non-food ads; Coke logo ads > non-food ads), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with correction for multiple comparisons (cluster-wise pFWE and 3dClustSim), and presents whole-brain results in tables and text. Relevant methodological details are provided (participant characteristics/age and sex in Table 1, cue type = food/soft drink, 3T Siemens Allegra scanner, SPM8 preprocessing, AFNI modules for cluster correction). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in children. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing high-calorie vs low-calorie (and uses blurred images as baseline), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA) with cluster correction. The paper provides participant age and sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3.0T), and processing software (AFNI). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking and neutral pictures). The manuscript reports within-subject contrasts (craving versus neutral) and other task contrasts, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses performed in SPM8 with cluster-level correction (reported coordinates and cluster statistics). Relevant participant information (age, all-male sample), cue type (smoking/nicotine), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Verio) and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (milkshake vs tasteless cue images). It reports within-participant contrasts of unpaired milkshake cue > unpaired tasteless cue and milkshake receipt > tasteless receipt. Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted in SPM5 (second-level regressions and ANOVAs) and results are reported as peak coordinates/tables (Tables 2 and 3) with small-volume corrections, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported in the paper. Participant age/sex (young adult females), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Provided 'full text' is only a website privacy/cookie notice; core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is missing. Therefore I cannot verify any required methodological details. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (cannot confirm this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli from the available content), I4 (cannot confirm within-participant contrast of reward cues>control), I5 (cannot confirm presence of group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps), I6 (cannot confirm reporting of whole-brain results in text/figures/tables), I7 (insufficient reporting of participant age, scanner field strength, processing software — title only indicates female participants and a beverage cue but does not satisfy I7). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 can be assessed from the truncated content. Because the full text is incomplete, the study cannot be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of high-calorie and low-calorie foods and neutral images). Within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie and high-calorie > neutral) are reported. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses were performed and reported (SPM T maps, voxel-level thresholds, cluster coordinates, tables and figures). Relevant methodological details are reported: cue type (food), MRI field strength (3 T), processing software (SPM5), and participant sex (two women, one man); participants are described as adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI study using visual fractal cues to probe responses to food rewards (a natural reward). It reports within-subject contrasts comparing reward-predictive cues versus reward-omission cues (cue-phase contrasts), satisfying a cue>control within-participant contrast. The paper includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-threshold corrected maps, tables/figures) and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3 T), and preprocessing software (BrainVoyager). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract), so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward (food) cues with within-participant contrasts of food>control (food vs nonfood objects). The full text reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects activation maps for the food vs control contrast (voxelwise maps presented and described, with cluster-level correction), and also provides ROI analyses. Participant age/sex (females 18–35), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are explicitly reported. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not report only ROI or connectivity analyses, and it includes an unmasked whole-brain task effect. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are satisfied and the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). It includes within-subject contrasts of food>neutral (food minus neutral) and reports those analyses (I4). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM5 with whole-brain correction and reported results/coordinates (I5, I6). The paper reports participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5) (I7). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and references; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This paper is a study protocol/trial methods manuscript that describes planned fMRI paradigms and analyses using visual food cues, but does not report any original human fMRI results or present group-level whole-brain task-activation maps or coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study paradigm with natural reward visual cues—food) and I4 (planned within-participant contrasts of food>control). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps in the manuscript), I7 (processing software for fMRI analyses is not reported). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (non-empirical/protocol paper without original human fMRI data). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food cues>control (e.g., Look Craved > Look Neutral and Look Craved > Look Not Craved), and whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses with corrected thresholds and reported activation clusters. Methods include scanner field strength (3.0T) and processing software (SPM8); participant age/sex and cue type (food) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-participant contrasts (fattening vs. non-fattening food images) with detailed participant info, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL/AFNI/FreeSurfer). However, the neuroimaging results are reported using an a priori ROI approach and averaged ROI parameter estimates; the paper does not present or describe any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or tables/coordinates of whole-brain results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (group-level whole-brain map) and I6 (no whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of natural reward visual cues), I4 (within-participant contrast of reward>control), I7 (reported age/sex, cue type, field strength, processing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain map), I6 (no whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food vs neutral images). It includes within-participant contrasts of food>neutral, reports group-level whole-brain analyses (task PLS and SPM GLM with reported clusters/coordinates), and provides participant demographics, cue type (food), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM5). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that examines neural responses to stimuli paired with methamphetamine versus placebo. It uses visual (plus auditory) cues and reports within-subject contrasts comparing methamphetamine-paired to placebo-paired cues. The paper includes a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain ANCOVA (AFNI 3dmvm) with cluster-level inference and reports significant clusters in tables/figures/text. Participant age range and sex are reported; MRI field strength (3.0 T) and processing software (AFNI) are specified. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity using visual drug cues and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using visual cues (chocolate picture, mouldy drink) to probe natural reward- and aversion-related cue-reactivity. It reports within-participant contrasts of cue>control (pleasant/unpleasant cue vs grey image), group-level whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses (SPM8) with whole-brain cluster/FWE correction, and provides MNI coordinates, figures, participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task activation maps). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3–I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study investigates appetitive (natural reward) conditioning using erotic (sexual) visual stimuli and reports within-participant contrasts (CS+ > CS− and erotic pictures > control). The paper includes group-level whole-brain analyses (whole-brain results for CS+ > CS− are reported) alongside ROI analyses, and reports coordinates and statistics. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity meta-analysis of natural reward visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study using visual conditioned cues predicting a natural reward (juice) and neutral/aversive liquids, and it performs within-subject/model-based contrasts relating cue responses to prediction-error/value signals (so I3, I4, I6, and I7 are met). However, the fMRI acquisition used restricted/zoomed coverage focused on midbrain and nearby regions rather than whole-brain coverage; although group-level voxelwise results are reported for the acquired volume, the study does not provide a true whole-brain (full-brain) group-level task-evoked statistical map as required by I5. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual natural-reward stimuli (infant faces) in mothers with substance addiction. It reports within-participant contrasts of own-happy > unknown-happy (natural reward cue > control), and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster thresholds and Talairach coordinates. Participant age and sex (postpartum mothers; ages reported), cue type (infant faces as natural reward), MRI scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX v2.3.1) are all reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The authors report a within-participant contrast of food cues versus control stimuli (people/nature scenes) and entered these contrasts into second-level random-effects (group-level) whole-brain analyses. They report MNI coordinates for ROIs used, scanner field strength (3T), processing software (SPM8), participant age and sex (31 females, mean age 21.1), and cue type (food). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the meta-analysis scope and all inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI study using visual natural-reward (food) cues in children (I3). The design included within-participant contrasts using food and non-food control stimuli (furniture/blurred) (I4). Analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps with cluster correction and reported peak coordinates (I5; I6). The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager) (I7). Results include whole-brain contrasts (e.g., High-ED vs Low-ED, large vs small portions) and peak coordinates in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state-only; includes within-subject task effects and whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts (food > nonfood and high-calorie > nonfood) and group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with reported peak coordinates and cluster statistics (Table 1, figures). Whole-brain voxelwise maps were used with small-volume correction within predefined ROIs and results (coordinates and corrected p-values) are clearly described in the text/tables. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

The meta-analysis requires fMRI cue-reactivity studies that use visual stimuli (Inclusion I3). This study used an alcohol taste (oral) cue paradigm (Alcohol Taste > Water Taste), not visual cues, so it does not meet I3. The full text is complete and reports within-participant contrast (Alcohol>Water) (I4), whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (I5/I6), and provides participant demographics, cue type (alcohol taste), scanner strength and processing software details (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded solely because it fails to satisfy I3 (use of visual stimuli).

The study is excluded because it does not assess fMRI cue-reactivity to visual drug/natural reward cues. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (relevant participant info, cue type 'food', scanner field strength 3T, processing software SPM8 reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (the fMRI component measured resting CBF changes after intranasal insulin vs placebo rather than visual cue-reactivity), I4 (no within-participant contrast of visual reward cues > control during fMRI; food pictures were rated outside the scanner and not used in a voxelwise task contrast), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map of cue-reactivity contrasts), I6 (not applicable because no cue-reactivity whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were specifically triggered by the text. Full text appears complete for screening.

The full text describes an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (chocolate) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (chocolate vs neutral pictures). It includes within-participant contrasts (chocolate > neutral) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (F-maps) and cluster-based fROIs, with Talairach coordinates in tables/figures. Relevant participant (female sample), cue type (food/chocolate), MRI field strength (3-T Siemens Allegra), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task activations). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts of sexual > neutral (supraliminal and subliminal) reported at the group level. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial and contrasts) with tables/figures of activations and coordinates, thresholding, and ROI follow-ups. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (sexual), MRI field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis: it is an fMRI study of reward anticipation using the monetary incentive delay (MID) task rather than a visual cue-reactivity paradigm with drug or natural reward images. Specifically: (a) exclusion IDs met: none (no E3–E6 violations detected). (b) inclusion IDs met: I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps with coordinates/figures), I6 (whole-brain results reported in coordinates and figures), I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type as monetary reward, MRI field strength [3T], and processing software [SPM8]). (c) inclusion IDs NOT met: I3 (does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimulus images typical of cue-reactivity paradigms), I4 (primary contrast was anticipation of large reward vs baseline rather than an explicit within-participant contrast of reward/drug cues > control stimuli). Therefore exclude.

The study is EXCLUDED because it does not assess cue-reactivity to visual drug or natural-reward cues. Specifically: (a) Exclusion IDs met: none of E3–E6 apply. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I7 (the paper reports participant age and sex, cue type = food, MRI field strength = 3T, and processing software = SPM5). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (not a task fMRI study of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli — this is a resting/physiologic ASL comparison after high- vs low-GI meals), I4 (no within-participant contrast of cue > control stimuli; the within-subject contrast is meal condition, not cue exposure), I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for cue-reactivity; analyses reflect resting cerebral blood flow differences tied to meal condition), and I6 (not applicable because no cue-evoked whole-brain results are presented). Full text is complete and sufficient to make this determination.

This article is a narrative review of orbitofrontal cortex involvement in substance abuse that summarizes prior PET and fMRI studies; it does not present original empirical human fMRI data or new voxelwise, group-level whole-brain task activation maps. Exclusion: E6 (non-empirical review) applies. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an original fMRI study assessing cue-reactivity with visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cues>control contrast reported as an original analysis), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map presented as original results), I7 (no original participant age/sex, MRI field strength, or processing software reported for a primary fMRI experiment). Although the review discusses visual cue-reactivity studies, it is a secondary synthesis rather than an eligible empirical fMRI study, so it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E3 met: the study did not acquire whole-brain images and reports ROI-focused analyses (small-volume correction in ventral striatum) without an unmasked, whole-brain task-activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts of reward cue > neutral were conducted: anticipation of gain/loss vs neutral) and I7 (relevant methodological/participant info reported: age/sex counts, cue type [monetary], scanner field strength 1.5T, and processing software SPM5). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not assess drug cues or the listed natural reward cue types [food/sexual] specified by the review — it uses monetary incentives), I5 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task map was provided), and I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported as tables/figures since whole-brain data were not acquired). Because E3 is violated and required whole-brain evidence is lacking, the study must be excluded.

This published empirical fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. I3: It is an fMRI study of natural reward (monetary) cue-reactivity using visual incentive cues (MID task). I4: It reports within-participant contrasts of reward cues > control (contrast: ¥20+¥100+¥500 > ¥0) for anticipation. I5: It includes group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (whole-brain results reported at voxel p<0.001, cluster FWE-corrected p<0.05). I6: Whole-brain results are described in text and figures/tables. I7: Relevant methodological/participant details are reported (age range 25–39 given; MRI field strength 1.5T; processing with SPM8; participant demographics are referenced in Table 1). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; tables/figures are referenced. Therefore include in the review.

The study is an fMRI study of food (natural reward) and reports participant age/sex and cue type (food), so it meets I3 and I7. However, it does NOT include any within-participant cue>control contrast (no task-based visual cue-reactivity contrast during fMRI); the fMRI measured hypothalamic response to oral glucose ingestion, not to visual food cues presented during scanning. Analyses were ROI-based (manual hypothalamic region) on a single midsagittal slice rather than group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. This also triggers exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of anticipatory responses to monetary (natural) reward cues using visual cues and within-subject contrasts (gain > neutral), and reports participant demographics, scanner (3T), and processing software (AFNI). However, the imaging results are reported using ROI / small-volume-corrected analyses within predefined mesocorticolimbic regions; the manuscript does not present or describe an unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map (results and multiple-comparison correction are reported within ROIs/SVC). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E3. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I7. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no unmasked whole-brain group-level voxelwise task map); I6 not applicable because I5 not satisfied. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study using visual monetary cues (MID task) assessing reward-related cue-reactivity with within-subject contrasts (gain cues > neutral), and reports group-level whole-brain task activation results (voxelwise maps with cluster-level FWE correction) as well as ROI results. Methods report participant sex (9 males, 10 females), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM8); demographic table (Table 1) is referenced for participant age. Therefore the paper satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, provides within-participant contrasts, whole-brain group maps (reported in text/tables/figures), and the required methodological details. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This article is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol vs neutral and other categories) analyzed with a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM/ANOVA (cluster-level correction) and presents coordinates and figures (Table 2, figures). Methods report scanner field strength (Philips 3T), processing software (BrainVoyager QX), cue type (alcohol), and participant demographics are described with reference to Table 1 (group sizes, tests for age/education/sex differences). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This study is a resting-state fMRI pharmacological challenge examining naltrexone effects on intrinsic functional connectivity; it does not involve any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm or presentation of visual drug/natural reward cues. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state connectivity analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type not applicable but reports MRI field strength and processing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a task fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control stimulus contrasts), I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is a resting-state seed-based functional connectivity investigation relating visceral adiposity to insular networks and food craving. It did not acquire or analyze an fMRI task involving visual cue exposure during scanning: food photographs were presented after the resting-state scan and craving ratings were collected post-scan. Therefore there is no within-participant task contrast (e.g., food cues > control) nor any group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported. It thus fails key inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity task fMRI studies and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only seed-based/resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). The paper does report participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8), so I7 is satisfied. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because E4 applies and inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5 (and therefore I6 as there is no task map to report) are not met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol-related cue-reactivity using visual cues (abstract geometric shapes predicting beer vs water). It includes within-participant contrasts (beer>water) during anticipation, outcome notification, and delivery phases. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (T-maps, cluster-level FWE correction) and provides activation coordinates and neurovault links (i.e., qualifying whole-brain results). Relevant metadata are reported (participant age/sex, cue type: alcohol, 3T scanner, processing software SPM8). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This article is a non-empirical review (not original human fMRI data) and therefore meets exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria I3–I7 are not met: the paper does not report an empirical fMRI study of drug/natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3), contains no within-participant drug-cue>control contrasts (I4), provides no whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps (I5/I6), and does not report participant- or imaging-specific details required (I7). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/introduction and references provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (alcohol, marijuana, polydrug, and appetitive images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts for alcohol>neutral and appetitive>neutral (cue reactivity contrasts). Methods describe group-level, mixed-effects, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with cluster-based thresholding for the cue reactivity task (i.e., task-evoked statistical maps were produced). Participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3.0T), and processing software (FSL v5.0) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes original human fMRI data). Full text contains intro, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug-related) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol advertisement images) with a within-participant contrast (ALCOHOL > CONTROL). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-based multiple-comparisons correction and peak coordinates (satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting in tables/figures). Participant age and sex are reported (college sample, ages 18–22, sex counts), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8; AFNI used for cluster correction) are specified. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual nicotine-related (e-cigarette) advertising stimuli presented to adolescents. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of e-cigarette>neutral images, and a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis (AFNI) with multiple-comparison correction; activations are reported in tables/figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine/e-cigarette), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food pictures) with within-participant contrasts (food vs. non-food; high-calorie vs. non-food). Group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses were conducted in SPM8 with whole-brain normalization and voxelwise inference; results are reported with FWE correction (small-volume correction for a priori ROIs) and coordinates/figures are presented. Participant age range and sex matching, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0T GE Signa HDxt), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual images of food (natural reward) and reports within-subject contrasts (appetizing > bland; appetizing > nonfood) at the group (random-effects) level with voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain random-effects contrasts and regression analyses are reported with coordinate tables and figures; processing software (SPM99), scanner field strength (3T), participant age and sex, and cue type (food) are all provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text is a 3T fMRI empirical study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps with necessary methodological details (age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, SPM8), satisfying I3, I5, I6, and I7. However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4). The task contrasts compare regulation strategies (LATER vs NOW) for food images and treatment (OXT vs PLC), and while some contrasts are tested versus low-level baseline, there is no analysis of food cues compared to neutral/control visual stimuli, so the key cue-reactivity contrast required by the meta-analysis is absent. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine-related visual cue-reactivity in smokers using pictorial stimuli and an attentional-bias task. It includes a within-subject contrast of smoking vs neutral pictures (LCSP minus LCNP), reports group-level random-effects analyses (RM-ANOVA and between-group t-tests) and provides coordinates/figures for task-evoked activation (with small-volume correction within a priori ROIs). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes unmasked between-group task effect for placebo). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion reason: The paper is an fMRI study of visual food cues (natural reward) and includes within-subject contrasts (food > nonfood), but it reports results using small-volume correction within predefined ROIs and does not present an unambiguous group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain coordinates/figures outside ROI-focused SVC. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrasts of food cues > control nonfood stimuli). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map reported) and I7 (insufficient reporting of participant sex in the full text as provided; age and scanner/software are reported but sex breakdown is not clearly stated). Full text assessed appears complete for core content. Based on failure to meet I5 and I7 and meeting exclusion E3, exclude from meta-analysis.

Full text for this article is not available in the provided content (only a redirect/placeholder page). I cannot verify whether this is an fMRI study using visual drug or natural reward cues, whether it reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., food cues > control), or whether it provides group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) maps and required methodological details. Therefore I must exclude due to inability to confirm inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual cues (photographs of the beloved vs a familiar neutral person) that probes natural reward–related cue reactivity (romantic/attachment craving). It includes within-participant contrasts (rejecter > neutral). Group-level, voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM2 (mixed-effects GLM) and whole-brain exploratory thresholds were reported with coordinate tables (P < 0.001 uncorrected, clusters ≥15 voxels), satisfying the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task map reported in the text/tables. Relevant metadata are reported (participant age/sex, cue type described, scanner field strength 1.5 T, processing software SPM2). Although some activations did not survive whole-brain correction, the paper provides whole-brain voxelwise results (coordinates) and meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study investigates food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual cues (abstract snack baskets vs empty basket and wallet images) and includes within-subject contrasts of high vs no food reward (10 SP vs 0 SP) during anticipation and receipt phases. The authors report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation analyses (cluster-level corrected results and supplementary tables of activations) and also ROI analyses; whole-brain results are clearly described. Relevant details are provided: participant demographics (age ranges, group sizes, sex matched), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM8). Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of food-related cues (high- and low-caloric food picture responses) relative to baseline across conditions (post-load minus basal), with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (four-way repeated-measures ANOVA) and tables/figures of results. Participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. Whole-brain results are presented (coordinates, maps) rather than ROI-only analyses. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study used gustatory (taste) alcohol cues (alcohol taste vs litchi juice) rather than visual stimuli, so it fails inclusion criterion I3 (visual-stimulus cue-reactivity). It does satisfy I4 (within-participant alcohol>control contrasts), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps using FLAME/FSL), I6 (reports whole-brain results in figures/tables), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3-T), and processing software (FSL)). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).
